content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VI ENGLISH — UNIT 5KNOWING CHILDREN FROM OTHER NATIONS(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 5: KNOWING CHILDREN FROM OTHER NATIONS (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 5.1 Reading Comprehension: Letters from International Pen-Pals
Exploring international friendships, cultures, and geography:
Pre-Reading Q1. What is a Pen-Pal?
Ans: A pen-pal is a friend with whom one builds a friendship and regularly exchanges letters or emails, often living in another city or foreign country.
Pre-Reading Q2. Why is it beneficial to learn about children living in other nations?
Ans: Learning about children in other countries broadens our mental horizons, teaches us about different cultures, traditions, and geography, and fosters global brotherhood and peaceful harmony.
Pre-Reading Q3. Can you name three foreign countries and their capital cities?
Ans: Yes: (1) Japan (Capital: Tokyo); (2) Turkey (Capital: Ankara); (3) Kenya (Capital: Nairobi).
Pre-Reading Q4. What comes to your mind when you hear the words 'Culture' and 'Tradition'?
Ans: Culture and tradition represent the shared customs, clothing, languages, traditional foods, architectural monuments, and spiritual celebrations of a community or nation.
■ WHILE-READING EXERCISE 1–3: MEET THE INTERNATIONAL PEN-PALS
Q: Name the three pen-pals introduced in the reading text and their home countries.

Ans: The three international pen-pals are:1. Kenji — a 12-year-old boy living in Kyoto, Japan.2. Ayse — an 11-year-old girl living in Istanbul, Turkey.3. Kwame — a 12-year-old boy living in Nairobi, Kenya.
A. Native animals and plants living in natural habitats
1 — C (traditional Japanese long robe with wide sleeves)
B. Warm, generous, and welcoming treatment of guests
2 — D (the customs, arts, and social habits of a nation)
C. A traditional Japanese loose garment tied with a sash
3 — A (wild animals such as lions, zebras, and elephants)
D. The customs, beliefs, and social behaviour of a people
4 — E (an easily recognized prominent building or feature)
E. A prominent, well-known building or geographic feature
5 — F (such as the Blue Mosque or Mount Kenya)
F. Generous, friendly reception and entertainment of guests
6 — B (a hallmark of both Turkish and Pakistani cultures)
■ POST-READING EXERCISE 6: INTERNATIONAL PEN-PALS COMPARISON TABLE
Kimono robe; Sushi, Rice, Miso soup
Embroidered vests, scarves; Kebab, Baklava, Tea
Blue Mosque, Bosphorus Bridge; Republic Day
Colourful Shuka wrap; Ugali, Roasted maize
Nairobi National Park, Mount Kenya; Safari Week
Q1. What makes Kyoto such an attractive and historical city in Japan?
Ans: Kyoto is famous for its ancient wooden temples, serene Zen gardens, historic imperial palaces, and the stunning bloom of pink cherry blossoms every spring.
Q2. Why does Ayse describe Istanbul as a unique bridge between two worlds?
Ans: Istanbul is historically unique because it physically bridges two continents—Asia and Europe—separated by the magnificent Bosphorus Strait.
Q3. What exciting natural wonders did Kwame describe about his homeland Kenya?
Ans: Kwame described the Great Rift Valley, snow-capped Mount Kenya near the equator, and wildlife reserves where herds of lions, zebras, giraffes, and cheetahs roam freely in the wild.
Q4. What common values do children across all these different nations share?
Ans: Despite differences in language, climate, and clothing, all children cherish family love, enjoy sports and creative arts, value peaceful friendship, and strive for good education.
Q5. How does having international pen-pals promote global peace?
Ans: Exchanging letters dispels harmful stereotypes, builds empathy, promotes mutual respect for different customs, and helps young people realize that humanity is one big global family.

When discussing international traditions, we should show deep respect and open-mindedness: 'That is such a fascinating tradition', 'I find your country's history truly admirable', 'While our customs differ, we share the same human values'.

• Dialogue 1 (Comparing dietary habits):Farooq: 'Kenji, how do you eat rice with wooden chopsticks without dropping grains?'Kenji: 'It takes patience and practice from early childhood! In Japan, eating with chopsticks is considered an art of mindfulness and gratitude for nature's food.'

• Dialogue 2 (Cultural hospitality):Ayse: 'In Turkey, whenever a guest arrives, we immediately serve hot tulip-shaped cups of black tea with sweet pistachios and Turkish delight.'Fatima: 'That is exactly like Pakistan! In our culture, hospitality is a sacred duty, and we welcome guests with warm milk tea and cardamom sweets.'
► 5.3 Language Practice: Passive Voice & Prepositions of Time
■ EXERCISE 1–3: PASSIVE VOICE (PRESENT & PAST SIMPLE TRANSFORMATIONS)
Kenji wears a traditional kimono on festivals.
A traditional kimono is worn by Kenji on festivals.
Ayse baked sweet baklava for her guests.
Sweet baklava was baked by Ayse for her guests.
Breathtaking wildlife photographs were taken by Kwame.
Millions of tourists visit Istanbul every year.
Istanbul is visited by millions of tourists every year.
The Japanese celebrate the Cherry Blossom festival.
The Cherry Blossom festival is celebrated by the Japanese.
■ EXERCISE 4–6: PREPOSITIONS OF TIME (AT, ON, IN, DURING, BEFORE, AFTER)
• Use 'at' for specific clock times and festivals: at 5:00 pm, at dawn, at Eid, at night.
• Use 'on' for specific days and dates: on Monday, on 23rd March, on my birthday.
• Use 'in' for months, years, centuries, and seasons: in July, in 2026, in the 21st century, in winter.
• Use 'during' for periods of time: during the summer vacation, during the match.
• Use 'before / after' for relative timing: before sunset, after school.
Solved Sentence: 1. Kenji's school starts **at** 8:30 am sharp every morning.
Solved Sentence: 2. The annual Cherry Blossom festival takes place **in** April.
Solved Sentence: 3. Ayse and her family celebrate Republic Day **on** 29th October.
Solved Sentence: 4. Kwame visited the national wildlife reserve **during** the winter break.
Solved Sentence: 5. Students must wash their hands **before** eating lunch and **after** sports.
► 5.4 Writing: A Student's Autobiography ('My Journey as a Student')
• Model Autobiography: My Journey as a Student

My name is Muhammad Hamza, and I was born in Karachi, the bustling coastal metropolis of Pakistan. I am currently twelve years old and studying in Class VI at Government Boys Secondary School. Growing up in a hardworking, loving family, my parents instilled in me a deep love for truth, honesty, and knowledge from an early age.

My school days are filled with excitement and learning. My favourite academic subjects are English and General Science. I love reading adventure stories, discovering how the human body functions, and experimenting with simple science models. During recess and after school, my passion is playing cricket with my classmates in the school ground. I am a right-handed opening batsman and the vice-captain of our class team.

Life is not without challenges. Last year, I struggled with mathematics geometry, but with patient guidance from my teacher and dedicated daily practice, I scored top marks in my final examination. My ultimate dream is to become a software engineer so that I can develop educational computer programs for underprivileged children across Pakistan. I believe that with faith in Allah, relentless hard work, and patience, every honest dream can turn into reality!
► 5.5 Study Skills: The Free Writing Technique

Free Writing is a creative pre-writing exercise where you write continuously for 10 minutes without stopping to edit, correct spelling, or worry about grammar. It unlocks creativity, overcomes writer's block, and allows ideas to flow freely from the subconscious mind.
• Sample Free Writing: If I Could Travel Anywhere
Topic: 'If I Could Travel Anywhere in the World'

If I had an airplane ticket right now I would definitely fly to Istanbul in Turkey because the pictures of the Bosphorus Strait look so magical with ferries gliding across blue water between Europe and Asia. I want to walk inside the Blue Mosque and touch the ancient tiles and hear the melodious Azan echoing over the domes. Then I want to visit the Grand Bazaar and taste warm Turkish baklava dripping with honey and pistachios. After that I would love to travel to Japan to ride the Shinkansen bullet train that goes at 300 km per hour without shaking a single drop of water in a glass. Meeting children from other nations would be wonderful because we could exchange coins, stamps, and learn words in Turkish and Japanese. Traveling teaches us that the world is a colourful garden where every nation is a unique, fragrant flower.
► 5.6 Fun Time: Fun with Verbs (Action Words Challenge)

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VI ENGLISH — UNIT 6LEARNING THROUGH PERSONAL INTERESTS, ABILITIES AND HOBBIES(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 6: LEARNING THROUGH PERSONAL INTERESTS, ABILITIES AND HOBBIES (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
Discovering personal strengths, creative hobbies, and overcoming shyness:
Pre-Reading Q1. What is a hobby or personal interest?

Ans: A hobby is an enjoyable, productive activity or leisure pursuit that a person pursues in their spare time for relaxation, self-expression, and personal development (e.g., painting, gardening, reading, coding, calligraphy).
Pre-Reading Q2. Have you ever felt shy, hesitant, or thought that you had no special talent?

Ans: Many young people occasionally feel hesitant or compare themselves with others. However, every human being is blessed with unique latent abilities waiting to be discovered through practice and encouragement.
Pre-Reading Q3. Who helps students discover and nurture their hidden talents?
Ans: Loving parents, inspiring teachers, elder mentors, and supportive friends play an essential role in recognizing and nurturing a child's hidden potentials.
Pre-Reading Q4. Look at the title 'Yes, You Can'. What inspiring message does it convey?
Ans: It conveys an uplifting message of self-belief, confidence, and determination. With self-trust and patient guidance, anyone can overcome self-doubt and accomplish great things.
Q: Why was Zainab initially sad and dejected in the story?

Ans: Zainab felt dejected because her classmates were talented in drama, speech contests, and sports, while she believed that she had no special talent or ability to showcase at the upcoming school exhibition.
A. The state of having faith in oneself and one's abilities
1 — C (the artistic visual craft of decorative beautiful handwriting)
B. Feeling unsure, slow to speak, or reluctant to act
2 — A (belief in one's own power to succeed)
C. The visual art of producing decorative, beautiful handwriting
3 — E (words of praise, support, and motivation from teacher)
D. Warm approval, high respect, and praise from others
4 — F (being the only one of its kind; special and distinct)
E. Support, inspiration, and confidence given to someone
5 — B (slow, shy, and doubtful about participating)
F. Being one of a kind, exceptional, and distinctly special
6 — D (feeling of delighted approval and respect from judges)
■ POST-READING EXERCISE 6: TRUE OR FALSE STATEMENTS
Zainab's teacher discouraged her and told her to sit quietly in the back.
False — Her art teacher, Ms. Yasmin, noticed her neat handwriting, encouraged her warmly, and offered to teach her calligraphy.
Calligraphy requires special bamboo pens (qalam), ink, and patient practice.
True — Calligraphy is a sacred traditional art requiring specialized bamboo reed pens, smooth handmade paper, and meticulous practice.
Zainab gave up after her first practice session because her lines were crooked.
False — Zainab remembered the lesson of patience, practiced for two hours every evening, and steadily perfected her brush strokes.
Zainab's calligraphic artwork won the prestigious first prize and a gold medal.
True — Her framed Quranic verse in elegant Thuluth script won first prize and broad praise at the district exhibition.
The story shows that self-confidence and patient practice can uncover hidden talents.
True — The central moral is that every student possesses unique strengths that blossom with belief and hard work.
Q1. How did Ms. Yasmin discover that Zainab had a special flair for calligraphy?
Ans: While reviewing homework notebooks, Ms. Yasmin noticed that Zainab's handwriting was remarkably neat, symmetrical, and naturally well-proportioned.
Q2. What tools and materials did Ms. Yasmin give Zainab to begin her artistic journey?
Ans: Ms. Yasmin gifted Zainab a set of carved bamboo pens (qalam), a bottle of traditional black ink, smooth practice sheets, and an introductory book of classical scripts.
Q3. How did Zainab's feelings change as the exhibition day approached?
Ans: Her initial hesitation and self-doubt transformed into joy, quiet pride, and deep self-confidence as she saw her calligraphy pieces taking breathtaking shape.
Q4. What was written on the frame of Zainab's winning art display?
Ans: Her masterwork featured the sacred verse 'Read! In the name of your Lord who created' written in magnificent, flowing gold and black script.
Q5. What valuable lesson did Zainab's classmates learn from her achievement?
Ans: Her classmates learned that quiet, humble students often harbor extraordinary talents, and that genuine dedication and perseverance always triumph.
• Speaking Focus: Ability and Inability Expressions
To express what we are able to do, we use 'can', 'am able to', or 'know how to'. To express what we cannot do yet, we say 'cannot', 'am unable to', or 'am learning how to'.

• Dialogue 1 (Expressing ability in sports):Tariq: 'Can you swim across the deep end of the swimming pool?'Zubair: 'Yes, I can! I took professional swimming lessons last summer and I can easily swim four laps.'

• Dialogue 2 (Expressing inability with a positive mindset):Sara: 'Are you able to speak Turkish or Japanese like our pen-pals?'Amina: 'I am unable to speak them fluently right now, but I know how to say hello and thank you! I am going to learn more online.'

• Dialogue 3 (Encouraging a classmate):Bilal: 'I cannot sketch human portraits at all; my drawings look clumsy.'Zainab: 'Don't say you cannot! You just need basic guidance. I can teach you the proportions of face sketching during art period.'
► 6.3 Language Practice: Wh- Questions, First Conditional & Punctuation
Asks about a thing, action, or idea
What art form did Zainab practice?
Zainab practiced the art of calligraphy.
Asks about a place or location
Where was the art exhibition held?
It was held in the central city arts council hall.
When did Zainab practice her pen strokes?
She practiced every afternoon after finishing homework.
Because she thought she lacked any special talent.
Which script did she master first?
She mastered the elegant Naskh script first.
Asks about manner, process, or degree
How did she win the gold medal?
Through patient daily practice and self-belief.
■ EXERCISE 4–6: FIRST CONDITIONAL SENTENCES (IF + PRESENT SIMPLE, WILL + VERB)
First Conditional Formula: If + Present Simple (condition), will + Base Verb (result). Used for real, likely future possibilities.
Conditional Sentence: 1. (If / you / practice daily, you / improve your skills)Solved: If you practice daily, you will improve your skills.
Conditional Sentence: 2. (If / Zainab / enters the competition, she / win an award)Solved: If Zainab enters the competition, she will win an award.
Conditional Sentence: 3. (If / we / do not believe in ourselves, we / fail to achieve our dreams)Solved: If we do not believe in ourselves, we will fail to achieve our dreams.
Conditional Sentence: 4. (The teacher / feel proud / if all students / participate in activities)Solved: The teacher will feel proud if all students participate in activities.

When Ms. Yasmin walked into the classroom, she smiled and said, "Dear students, believe in yourselves! If you work hard and never lose heart, Allah will bless your honest efforts." Zainab looked up, clutched her wooden qalam, and whispered, "Yes, I can do it!"
► 6.4 Writing: A School Interview with a Young Artist
Situation: An authentic interview conducted by the Student Editor of the school magazine with Zainab, the district calligraphy champion.
Reporter (Hamza): Assalam-o-Alaikum, Zainab! Congratulations on winning the District Gold Medal for Calligraphy. How does it feel?
Zainab: Wa Alaikum Assalam, Hamza! Thank you so much. I feel immensely grateful to Allah Almighty, my supportive parents, and especially Ms. Yasmin, who believed in me when I had zero confidence.
Reporter (Hamza): What was the most challenging part when you began learning Arabic and English calligraphy?
Zainab: In the beginning, controlling the flow of ink and cutting the tip of the bamboo qalam at the exact angle was very frustrating. My fingers would cramp, and ink would blot on the paper.
Reporter (Hamza): How did you overcome that frustration?

Zainab: I remembered our English lesson on 'Try Again'. I reminded myself that failure is no disgrace. I committed to practicing sixty lines every single afternoon until the strokes became smooth and natural.
Reporter (Hamza): What advice would you give to fellow students who feel they have no special talents?

Zainab: Never compare yourself to others or look down on your own abilities. Every person has a hidden spark. Try new hobbies, read good books, listen to your teachers, and always remember: 'Yes, you can!'
Reporter (Hamza): Thank you so much for your valuable time and inspiring words, Zainab!
Zainab: It was my absolute pleasure. Thank you!
► 6.5 Study Skills: My Priorities (The Urgent vs Important Matrix)
Effective students manage their time by dividing daily tasks into four quadrants based on Urgency and Importance:
Practical Examples for Class VI Students
Preparing for tomorrow's exam, treating a high fever
Daily reading, regular exercise, revising lessons
Dedicate quality daily time; key to success
Phone notifications, minor interruptions, TV noise
Minimize time spent; don't let it derail study
Mindless social media scrolling, excessive gaming
Strictly eliminate or reduce to small weekend leisure
► 6.6 Fun Time: Word Association Game & Word Ladder
Calligraphy: Keywords: Bamboo pen, black ink, parchment paper, Naskh script, beauty, patience
Sports: Keywords: Cricket, football, stamina, teamwork, fair play, referee, victory
Gardening: Keywords: Soil, seeds, water hose, sunshine, green leaves, blossoming flowers, earthworms
Reading: Keywords: Library, bookshelf, knowledge, adventures, vocabulary, imagination, enlightenment
Change one letter at a time to transform 'READ' into 'BOOK':
READ → HEAD → HEAR → BEAR → BEAK → BOOK!
(الف) قومی تہوار کسے کہتے ہیں؟جو تہوار پوری قوم مل کر مناتی ہے اسے قومی تہوار کہتے ہیں۔ یہ تہوار قومی اتحاد اور یکجہتی کی علامت ہوتے ہیں۔
(ب) چودہ اگست کے دن کی تیاریاں کس طرح کی جاتی ہیں؟گھروں، گلیوں اور بازاروں کو سجایا جاتا ہے۔ سبز ہلالی پرچم لہرائے جاتے ہیں اور چراغاں کیا جاتا ہے۔
(ج) اس دن کی تقریبات کا آغاز کس طرح ہوتا ہے؟تقریبات کا آغاز پرچم کشائی سے ہوتا ہے۔ اس کے بعد قومی ترانہ پڑھا جاتا ہے۔
(د) اس دن ہم اتنی خوشی کیوں مناتے ہیں؟اس دن ہمیں آزادی حاصل ہوئی تھی۔ یہ آزادی ہمارے بزرگوں کی قربانیوں کا نتیجہ ہے۔
(ہ) چودہ اگست کا دن ہمیں کیا یاد دلاتا ہے؟یہ دن ہمیں آزادی کی نعمت کی یاد دلاتا ہے۔ یہ ہمیں قربانی اور جدوجہد کا سبق دیتا ہے۔
(و) قومی ترانہ سنتے ہی ہم سب کیوں کھڑے ہو جاتے ہیں؟ہم قومی ترانے کا احترام کرتے ہیں۔ یہ قومی اتحاد اور محبتِ وطن کی علامت ہے۔
درج ذیل لفظوں کو اپنے جملوں میں استعمال کیجیے:

چہل پہل: یومِ آزادی پر شہر میں بہت چہل پہل ہوتی ہے۔گہما گہمی: بازاروں میں گہما گہمی بڑھ جاتی ہے۔سر بلند: ہمارا پرچم سر بلند رہتا ہے۔زرِق برق: لوگ زرِق برق لباس پہن کر آتے ہیں۔اہتمام: اسکول میں جشن کا خاص اہتمام کیا جاتا ہے۔جدوجہد: ہمارے بزرگوں نے آزادی کے لیے جدوجہد کی۔

یومِ آزادی پاکستان کا ایک اہم قومی تہوار ہے جو ہر سال 14 اگست کو منایا جاتا ہے۔ اس دن پاکستان ایک آزاد مملکت کے طور پر دنیا کے نقشے پر ابھرا۔ ہمارے بزرگوں نے آزادی حاصل کرنے کے لیے بے شمار قربانیاں دیں، اپنا سب کچھ قربان کیا اور سخت مشکلات برداشت کیں۔

یومِ آزادی کے موقع پر ملک بھر میں جوش و خروش پایا جاتا ہے۔ گھروں، گلیوں، بازاروں اور عمارتوں کو سبز ہلالی پرچموں اور جھنڈیوں سے سجایا جاتا ہے۔ سرکاری سطح پر پرچم کشائی کی جاتی ہے، قومی ترانہ پڑھا جاتا ہے اور مختلف تقریبات منعقد ہوتی ہیں۔ بچے اور بڑے سب اس دن کو خوشی سے مناتے ہیں۔
یہ دن ہمیں آزادی کی قدر، اتحاد، قربانی اور حب الوطنی کا پیغام دیتا ہے۔ ہمیں چاہیے کہ ہم اپنے وطن کی حفاظت کریں، اس کی ترقی کے لیے محنت کریں اور ایک ذمہ دار شہری بن کر پاکستان کا نام روشن کریں۔
اپنے دوست کے نام ایک خط لکھیں جس میں یومِ آزادی کی مختصر تفصیل بیان کریں۔

امید ہے کہ تم خیریت سے ہوگے اور اللہ تعالیٰ کے فضل سے ہر طرح سے محفوظ ہوگے۔ میں تمہیں اس خط کے ذریعے یومِ آزادی کے بارے میں مختصر تفصیل بتانا چاہتا ہوں۔ پاکستان ہر سال 14 اگست کو یومِ آزادی بڑے جوش و خروش سے مناتا ہے۔ اس دن ہمیں یاد آتا ہے کہ ہمارے بزرگوں نے بڑی قربانیوں کے بعد ہمیں ایک آزاد وطن دیا۔

یومِ آزادی کے موقع پر گھروں، گلیوں اور بازاروں کو سبز ہلالی پرچموں سے سجایا جاتا ہے۔ سرکاری عمارتوں پر پرچم کشائی کی جاتی ہے اور قومی ترانہ پڑھا جاتا ہے۔ مختلف تقریبات، تقاریر اور ملی نغموں کے ذریعے اس دن کی خوشی منائی جاتی ہے۔ یہ دن ہمیں اتحاد، قربانی اور حب الوطنی کا درس دیتا ہے۔
آخر میں اللہ تعالیٰ سے دعا ہے کہ وہ ہمارے پیارے وطن پاکستان کو ہمیشہ سلامت رکھے اور ترقی عطا فرمائے۔ جلد جواب کا منتظر رہوں گا۔والسلامتمہارا مخلص دوستحسنین۔
جواب:ماحول سے مراد ہمارے اردگرد کی فضا، زمین، پانی، ہوا، درخت، جانور اور وہ تمام چیزیں ہیں جو ہمیں گھیرے ہوئے ہوتی ہیں اور ہماری زندگی پر اثر انداز ہوتی ہیں۔
(ب) کیا ہمارے ماحول کو آلودگی سے نقصان پہنچتا ہے؟
جواب:جی ہاں، ہمارے ماحول کو آلودگی سے بہت نقصان پہنچتا ہے۔ آلودگی کی وجہ سے ہوا، پانی اور زمین خراب ہو جاتے ہیں، جس سے انسانوں، جانوروں اور پودوں کی صحت متاثر ہوتی ہے۔
(ج) ماحول کو آلودہ کرنے کے کچھ سبب کیا ہیں؟
جواب:ماحول کو آلودہ کرنے کے چند اسباب یہ ہیں:
گندے پانی کا ندی نالوں میں بہانا
(د) فضائی آلودگی کا سبب کیا ہے؟
جواب:فضائی آلودگی کا سبب کارخانوں، فیکٹریوں اور گاڑیوں سے نکلنے والا دھواں ہے۔ اس کے علاوہ کوڑا کرکٹ جلانا اور ایندھن کا زیادہ استعمال بھی فضائی آلودگی کا باعث بنتا ہے۔
(ہ) شور کی آلودگی کے کیا اثرات ہیں؟
جواب:شور کی آلودگی سے انسان کی سماعت متاثر ہوتی ہے، ذہنی دباؤ بڑھتا ہے، نیند خراب ہوتی ہے اور دل کے امراض پیدا ہو سکتے ہیں۔
(و) ہمیں فضائی آلودگی سے بچنے کے لیے کیا کرنا چاہیے؟
جواب:ہمیں فضائی آلودگی سے بچنے کے لیے:
گاڑیوں کا کم استعمال کرنا چاہیے
(ز) پانی کی آلودگی کے خاتمے میں آپ کا کیا کردار ہو سکتا ہے؟
جواب:میں پانی کو ضائع نہیں کروں گا، گندا پانی ندی نالوں میں نہیں بہاؤں گا، صفائی کا خیال رکھوں گا اور دوسروں کو بھی پانی کو صاف رکھنے کی تلقین کروں گا۔
❷ درج ذیل الفاظ کو جملوں میں استعمال کیجیے:
(الف) صفائیہمیں اپنے گھر اور اسکول کی صفائی کا خاص خیال رکھنا چاہیے۔
(ب) شجرکاریشجرکاری سے ماحول صاف اور خوبصورت بنتا ہے۔
(ج) آلودگیآلودگی انسانی صحت کے لیے بہت نقصان دہ ہے۔
(د) ماحولصاف ماحول صحت مند زندگی کی علامت ہے۔
(ہ) نقصانفضائی آلودگی سے پھیپھڑوں کو نقصان پہنچتا ہے۔❸ واحد کی جمع اور مذکر کی مؤنث لکھیے:
✔️ درست بیان (✓) کا نشان اور غلط بیان (✗) کا نشان لگائیے:
(الف) پانی اللہ تعالیٰ کی عظیم نعمت ہے۔✅ (✓)
(ب) فضائی آلودگی سے انسان کو فائدہ ہوتا ہے۔❌ (✗)
(ج) آلودگی کے معاشرے میں ہر طرح کی بیماریاں پھیل رہی ہیں۔✅ (✓)
(د) شور کرنا انسان کی صحت کے لیے مفید ہے۔❌ (✗)
(ہ) چاردیواری کا نقصان آلودگی کی وجہ سے ہوتا ہے۔❌ (✗)
(و) ماحول کی صفائی ہر شخص اہم کردار ادا کر سکتے ہیں۔✅ (✓)

اللہ تعالیٰ نے ہمیں ایک خوبصورت دنیا عطا کی ہے جس میں صاف ہوا، میٹھا پانی، سرسبز درخت اور رنگ برنگے پھول شامل ہیں۔ ہمارا ماحول ہماری زندگی کا اہم حصہ ہے۔ اگر ماحول صاف ہو تو انسان صحت مند اور خوشحال زندگی گزار سکتا ہے، لیکن اگر ماحول آلودہ ہو جائے تو بیماریاں اور مسائل جنم لیتے ہیں۔

آج کل تیز رفتار ترقی کے باعث ماحول آلودہ ہوتا جا رہا ہے۔ کارخانوں اور گاڑیوں سے نکلنے والا دھواں فضائی آلودگی کا سبب بنتا ہے۔ گندا پانی ندی نالوں میں بہانے سے پانی آلودہ ہو جاتا ہے۔ اسی طرح جگہ جگہ کوڑا کرکٹ پھینکنے سے زمین بھی گندی ہو جاتی ہے۔ شور شرابہ بھی آلودگی کی ایک قسم ہے جو انسان کی سماعت اور ذہنی سکون کو متاثر کرتا ہے۔

ماحولی صفائی کے لیے ہمیں کچھ اہم اقدامات کرنے چاہئیں۔ ہمیں کوڑا کرکٹ ہمیشہ کوڑے دان میں ڈالنا چاہیے۔ درخت لگانے اور شجرکاری کی مہم میں حصہ لینا چاہیے کیونکہ درخت ہوا کو صاف کرتے ہیں۔ پانی کو ضائع نہیں کرنا چاہیے اور گندا پانی صاف کیے بغیر ندیوں میں نہیں بہانا چاہیے۔ گاڑیوں کا کم استعمال اور صاف ایندھن کا استعمال بھی فضائی آلودگی کو کم کرتا ہے۔
حکومت کے ساتھ ساتھ ہر فرد کی ذمہ داری ہے کہ وہ ماحول کی صفائی میں اپنا کردار ادا کرے۔ اگر ہم سب مل کر کوشش کریں تو ہمارا ملک صاف، سرسبز اور خوبصورت بن سکتا ہے۔
آخر میں یہی کہا جا سکتا ہے کہ صاف ماحول صحت مند زندگی کی ضمانت ہے۔ ہمیں آج ہی سے عہد کرنا چاہیے کہ ہم اپنے ماحول کو صاف رکھنے میں بھرپور کردار ادا کریں گے۔

content.text: Computational thinking is a problem-solving method used to handle complex problems by breaking them down and identifying patterns.
Decomposition means breaking a complex problem into smaller, manageable parts to solve them individually.
What is the purpose of data abstraction?
Abstraction allows us to ignore non-essential details and focus on the important information to create a general model of a problem.
An algorithm is a set of step-by-step solutions that must be carried out in a specific order to solve a given problem.
What are the five essential properties of an algorithm?
The five properties are input specified, output specified, definiteness, effectiveness, and finiteness.
A flowchart is a pictorial or graphical representation of a set of instructions used to plan out programs.
Selection determines which path a program takes while running, usually implemented through IF-THEN-ELSE statements.
What is the difference between a finite and an infinite loop?
A finite loop ends on its own after a set number of times, while an infinite loop continues until an outside cause stops it.
What is a logical error in programming?
A logical error occurs when a program runs but produces the wrong result because the underlying logic is incorrect.
What is a function in computing?
A function is a pre-defined piece of code that performs a specific task and can be reused multiple times.
Decompose means breaking a complex problem into smaller parts.
The diamond symbol in a flowchart indicates a decision.
Iteration means doing something repeatedly in a program, like a loop.
The oval shape marks the 'Start' and 'Stop' points in a flowchart.
A syntax error occurs when a keyword is misspelled, or wrong punctuation is used.
The modulo (mod) operation returns the remainder of a division.
Pattern Matching involves finding similarities or patterns within a problem.
A parallelogram represents input or output in a flowchart.
Run-time errors are generally only detected during program execution, such as dividing by zero.
Algorithms are at the heart of all computer applications.
True: Decomposition helps in understanding how a bicycle works by examining its parts.
False: A rectangle is used to represent a decision in a flowchart (The diamond is used).
True: An algorithm must have a clear starting and ending point.
True: WHILE and FOR are common ways to repeat actions for a certain number of times.
False: Syntax errors occur when the logic of the program is wrong (This is a logical error).
True: Abstraction hides non-essential details but does not mean those details are unimportant.
False: An infinite loop will eventually stop on its own (It requires an outside cause to stop).
True: Flowcharts always begin and end with an oval shape.
True: Modulo 9 mod 2 results in a remainder of 1.
False: Input is not required for an algorithm (An algorithm requires one or more input values).
Which of these is NOT a pillar of computational thinking?i. Decomposition ii. Abstraction iii. Coding iv. Pattern matching
Which technique involves ignoring irrelevant details?i. Selection ii. Abstractioniii. Iteration iv. Decomposition
A flowchart symbol used for a process is:i. Diamondii. Rectangle iii. Oval iv. Arrow
What does the 'IF-THEN-ELSE' statement implement?i. Sequence ii. Selection iii. Iterationiv. Finiteness
Which error occurs if you write "2 + 2 * 2" and expect "8"?i. Logical ii. Syntaxiii. Run-timeiv. Input
A loop that repeats for a five-second timer is a:i. Finite loop ii. Infinite loop iii. Selection loop iv. Logical loop
The symbol for connecting shapes in a flowchart is:i. Oval ii. Diamond iii. Arrow iv. Rectangle
Sudoku is an example of which technique?i. Abstraction ii. Pattern matching iii. Iteration iv. Sequence
What property ensures an algorithm has a countable number of steps?i. Input ii. Effectiveness iii. Finitenessiv. Definiteness
The modulo of 5 mod 3 is:i. 1 ii. 2 iii. 3 iv. 0
Which symbol is used to represent 'Wait for toast to pop up' in a flowchart?i. Oval ii. Parallelogram iii. Diamond (Decision) iv. Rectangle
Which construct describes a progression of tasks following one another?i. Sequence ii. Selection iii. Iteration iv. Function
In game development, the main game frame is often an:i. Finite loop ii. Infinite loop iii. Abstraction iv. Error
Which of the following is an example of a pattern?i. The sky is blue ii. My parrot talks
iii. All bicycles have wheelsiv. I have a computer
What is 'COS' in a scientific calculator?i. A variableii. A function iii. A flowchart symbol iv. An error
Which error type is caused by dividing a number by zero?i. Syntax ii. Run-time iii. Logical iv. Abstraction
What is the first step in the tea-making algorithm?i. Add tea leaves ii. Turn on stove iii. Take a kettle iv. Wait for boil
Which process focuses on important information only?i. Abstraction ii. Flowcharts iii. Pseudocode iv. Programming
How are symbols connected in a flowchart?i. By numbers ii. By colours iii. By arrows iv. None
Which tool is a pictorial representation of a problem?i. Algorithm ii. Flowchart iii. Decompose iv. Selection
Task: Create a Flowchart for a simple daily activity: Brushing your teeth.
Step 1: Use an Oval to mark "Start".
Step 2: Use Parallelograms for inputs (e.g., Get toothbrush, Get toothpaste).
Step 3: Use Rectangles for processes (e.g., Put toothpaste on brush, Brush teeth).
Step 4: Use a Diamond for a decision (e.g., Are teeth clean? If No, repeat brushing; If Yes, move to next step).
Step 5: Use a Rectangle for the final process (e.g., Rinse mouth).
Step 6: Use an Oval to mark "Stop".
Task: Using the steps provided in the source, arrange these tasks into a logical sequence to complete a functional school admission flowchart.
If Yes, proceed to Admission Granted.
If No, proceed to Waitlist or End of Process.
Create a flowchart that represents the school admission process.
Understand how decisions and conditions (like availability of seats) affect the flow of the process.

Task: Work in a group to plan a trip to a museum. You must write a detailed algorithm and draw a flowchart for the activity, specifically identifying sub-tasks, necessary resources, and potential "bottlenecks" that might delay the trip.
Identify resources required for the trip: Transport, tickets, guide, museum map.
List sub-tasks: Collect money, book transport, confirm tickets, assign group leader, etc.
Identify bottlenecks: Limited tickets, late arrivals, transport delays.
Start → Collect money → Book transport → Confirm tickets → Assign group leader → Depart for museum → Explore → Return → End
Collaborate to create a plan for a group activity.
Identify potential obstacles (bottlenecks) and how they can be avoided.

Task: Study a provided flowchart that classifies animals as herbivores or carnivores. Trace the execution steps for different inputs, such as a "Lion" (meat eater) or an "Elephant" (plant eater), to determine which path the algorithm takes and what the final output will be.
The algorithm checks if the animal is a meat eater.
Since the Lion is a carnivore, the output will be "Carnivore".
The algorithm checks if the animal is a plant eater.
Since the Elephant is a herbivore, the output will be "Herbivore".
Practice tracing algorithms with real-world examples.
Understand how different inputs lead to different paths in a flowchart.

Task: Develop a flowchart and algorithm for grading students based on their marks. Use selection constructs (IF-THEN-ELSE) to assign grades: for example, Output "A" for scores of 85% or above, and "Try Again" for scores less than 40%.
Start → Input marks → IF marks ≥ 85 → Output "A"
Learn how selection constructs work in decision-making scenarios.
Design a grading system that is easy to implement and understand.

Task: Analyze a series of statements (e.g., "All bicycles have wheels" vs. "My friend has a computer") to identify which represent a pattern. Explain how finding these similarities helps in building a general model to solve complex problems more efficiently.
Identify the patterns in the following statements:
"All bicycles have wheels": This is a general pattern based on the category of bicycles. It defines a key characteristic of bicycles.
"My friend has a computer": This is a specific statement about an individual’s possession and doesn't define a general pattern.
Explain the significance of recognizing patterns:

Recognizing patterns helps in building general models that can be used to solve complex problems more efficiently. For example, once you know that all bicycles have wheels, you don't need to check each individual bicycle for wheels. Instead, you can make the assumption that all bicycles will have wheels.
Understand how pattern recognition leads to efficient problem-solving by applying generalizations.

content.text: Answer: Scratch is a game development platform that allows users to develop games of their choice by applying fundamental programming constructs using visual programming tools.
Question: What is the first step to take when starting to program a game?
Answer: The first step is to decide on the game type, the characters (sprites) you want to use, the backdrop, and the number of levels.
Question: What is a "Sprite" in Scratch?
Answer: An object that can be programmed to move and interact with other objects on the stage is called a sprite.
Question: What do x- and y-coordinates represent on the stage?

Answer: Coordinates represent an exact location. The x-coordinate (horizontal position) indicates how far left or right a sprite is, while the y-coordinate (vertical position) indicates how far up or down it is.
Question: What are the coordinate ranges for the Scratch stage?
Answer: The x-coordinate ranges from -240 to 240, and the y-coordinate ranges from -180 to 180.
Question: Where is the center of the stage located?
Answer: The center of the stage is referred to as (0, 0).
Question: How do you make a sprite move left or right using coordinates?
Answer: To move a sprite right, you change the x-coordinate by a positive number. To move it left, you change the x-coordinate by a negative number.
Question: How do you prevent a sprite from passing through walls in a maze game?

Answer: You must program the sprite to check for collisions. If it touches the maze wall sprite, it should be programmed to reverse its last action (e.g., move back by the same amount it just moved) to stay within the paths.
Question: What is a variable and how is it used for scoring?

Answer: A variable is a value that can change. To track a score, you create a variable named "Score" and program it to increase by a value (like 10) whenever a specific goal is reached, such as touching a reward sprite.
Question: How do you create a countdown timer in Scratch?

Answer: You create a variable (e.g., "Time Remaining"), set its initial value (e.g., 60), and use a loop that waits for 1 second before changing the variable by -1. The game stops once the value reaches zero.
Question: How can you quickly add movement code for multiple arrow keys?
Answer: You can right-click on an existing "if then" block and select duplicate to create a copy, then simply change the key pressed and the coordinate values (x or y) for the new direction.
Question: What is the benefit of uploading a maze image instead of drawing one?
Answer: To save time, you can upload a pre-designed maze image from a computer using the "upload sprite" option instead of designing your own maze sprite from scratch.
Scratch is a game development platform that allows users to create programs using visual programming tools.
The first step to starting a game is to decide on the game type, the characters, the backdrop, and the number of levels.
In Scratch, an object that can be programmed to move and interact is called a sprite.
A plan for a maze game should include a reward for the character after completing the maze.
Coordinates are numbers that represent an exact location on the stage.
The x-coordinate represents the sprite's horizontal position.
The y-coordinate is also referred to as the y position.
The range of the x-coordinate on the Scratch stage is from -240 to 240.
The range of the y-coordinate on the Scratch stage is from -180 to 180.
The center of the stage is located at coordinates (0, 0).
To move a sprite to the left, you must change its x-coordinate by a negative number.
To move a sprite up, you change its y-coordinate by a positive number.
You can quickly copy a block of code in the script area by right-clicking it and selecting duplicate.
Instead of drawing a maze, you can save time by uploading a maze image from your computer.
To ensure a sprite starts in the middle of the stage, you use the block go to x: 0 y: 0.
To prevent a character from passing through walls, you must program it to check for collisions.
A variable is a value that can change throughout the game, such as a player's score.
To create a scoring system, you must go to the variable block palette and click "make a variable."
A countdown timer is used to increase the appeal, engagement, and risk of a game.
To make a timer count down, you use a loop that waits for 1 second and then changes the variable by -1.
Scratch is a game development platform used to create games with visual programming tools. (True)
The first step in programming a game is to immediately start coding without choosing a character or backdrop. (False - The first step is to decide on the game type, characters, backdrop, and levels)
In a Flappy Bird game, the score increases by a value of 1 every time you pass an obstacle. (True)
A "Sprite" is an object in Scratch that can be programmed to move and interact. (True)
The x-coordinate represents a sprite's vertical position on the stage. (False - The x-coordinate represents the horizontal position, or how far left or right a sprite is)
The center of the Scratch stage is referred to as (0, 0). (True)
The range of the y-coordinate on the Scratch stage is from -240 to 240. (False - The y-coordinate range is -180 to 180; the x-coordinate range is -240 to 240)
To move a sprite to the right, you must change its x-coordinate by a positive number. (True)
To move a sprite down, you should change its y-coordinate by a positive number. (False - To move down, you change the y-coordinate by a negative number)
The "duplicate" option allows you to create a copy of a block of code to save time. (True)
It is impossible to upload a maze image from your computer; you must draw it yourself. (False - You can save time by uploading a maze image using the "upload sprite" option)
To keep a sprite in front of a maze, you can use the "go to front layer" block. (True)
Collisions are checked to prevent a sprite from travelling through walls. (True)
A variable is a fixed value that can never change during a game. (False - A variable is a value that can change, such as a score or timer)
To create a scoring system, you must click "make a variable" in the variable block palette. (True)

b) Decide on the game type, characters, backdrop, and number of levels.

d) Click the green flag to see what happens.

d) A visual representation of a variable.

a) Change x by a positive number.
b) Change x by a negative number.

a) Rewrite the code manually for every key.
b) Right-click the "if then" block and select "duplicate."
c) Upload a new sprite for each direction.
d) Delete the current block and start over.

a) To make the game last forever.
b) To raise the risks and increase engagement and appeal.
c) To decrease the score automatically.

b) Program the sprite to reverse its action if it touches the wall.

Objective: Understand and apply the x- and y-coordinate system.

Task: Move a sprite to the following four corners of the stage using the go to x: y: block: (240, 180), (-240, 180), (-240, -180), and (240, -180). Finally, program the sprite to return to the Origin (0,0) when the green flag is clicked.
Assessment Criteria: Accurate positioning and understanding of stage limits.
Objective: Program movement using keyboard inputs.
Task: Create a script that allows the "Orange Cat" sprite to move in all four directions (Up, Down, Left, Right) using the arrow keys.
Code Requirement: Use a forever loop containing four if then blocks. For the right arrow, change x by a positive number; for the left, change x by a negative number.
Assessment Criteria: Smooth movement in all four directions without glitches.
Objective: Develop a game plan and manage sprites.

Task: Sketch an algorithm for a maze game on paper, including the start point, end goal, and obstacles. In Scratch, rename the default "Sprite1" to "Player" and upload a maze image from the computer as a new sprite.
Assessment Criteria: Logical flow of the algorithm and correct sprite naming/importing.
Objective: Use sensing blocks to restrict movement.
Task: Program the player sprite so it cannot pass through the maze walls.
Logic: Use an if touching [Maze]? then block inside each movement script to reverse the action (e.g., if moving right by 5, move back by -5 upon collision).
Assessment Criteria: The sprite should "bounce" off walls and stay within the paths.
Objective: Program interaction between two sprites.
Task: Add an "Apple" sprite to the end of the maze. Set its size to 25% and program the player sprite to "say Hurrah!" for 2 seconds when it touches the apple.
Assessment Criteria: Successful detection of the goal sprite.
Task: Create a variable named "Score". Program the game so that the score starts at 0 and increases by 10 points every time the player touches the goal sprite.
Assessment Criteria: Correct use of the "Variables" block palette and functional score updates.
Objective: Create a functional timer to increase game difficulty.

Task: Create a variable called "Time Remaining" and set it to 60 seconds. Use a loop to decrease the time by 1 every second until it reaches zero, at which point the script should "stop all" and display a "Game Over" message.
Assessment Criteria: Accurate 1-second intervals and game termination at zero.
Objective: Manage visual presentation and sprite properties.

Task: Use the go to front layer block to ensure the player sprite is always visible on top of the maze. Additionally, use the set size to [] % block to scale the player so it fits perfectly within the maze paths without touching walls constantly.
Assessment Criteria: Visual clarity and appropriate character scaling for gameplay.
Practical 9: Cat and Mouse Chase (AI Logic)
Objective: Apply concepts of events and loops to a specific scenario.
Task: Design a program where a "Cat" sprite constantly "points towards" and moves towards the "Mouse" sprite (or the mouse pointer).
Condition: If the Cat touches the Mouse, play a sound effect for 1 second.
Assessment Criteria: Effective use of "point towards" and "move" blocks within a loop.
Objective: Use editor tools to improve coding efficiency.
Task: Program the first movement key (e.g., Up Arrow). Use the Right-click > Duplicate function to quickly create the scripts for the other three arrow keys, adjusting the values accordingly.
Assessment Criteria: Efficient use of the duplicate tool to create a complete, error-free 4-way movement script.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VII ENGLISH — UNIT 1EFFECTS OF ACTIONS ON ENVIRONMENT(1.1 Can We Do Anything? (Prose))
Ali and Saleem noticed heavy smoke and plastic garbage on their way to school.
Their English teacher, Ms. Sana, asked the students: 'Can we do anything to stop pollution?'
Students decided to take practical civic action instead of just complaining.
They formed clean-up squads, banned plastic bags in school, and planted shade trees.
Moral: Even small actions by school children can protect our mother earth.
■  2. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Heavy black exhaust from old buses causes severe air pollution.
Students cleaned the roadside and placed all garbage inside bins.
Dangerous exhaust fumes damage the tender lungs of school children.
Our school launched a clean-and-green campaign in the neighborhood.
We can recycle used notebook paper to protect forests from felling.
Practical civic action is far better than merely complaining about dirt.
Keeping public parks tidy is an important civic responsibility.
Responsible citizens never litter wrapper plastics on streets.
Ali planted a young neem sapling in the school front yard.
Planting leafy trees keeps our living environment clean and fresh.
■  3. DICTATION WORDS (20 DIFFICULT SPELLINGS WITH URDU MEANINGS)
Q1:  What problem did Ali and Saleem observe on their way to school?
Ans:  They observed black smoke from old buses and piles of rotting plastic garbage along the road.
Q2:  What question did Ms. Sana ask her students?
Ans:  She asked: 'Can we do anything practical as students to clean our environment?'
Q3:  What steps did the students take in their school campaign?
Ans:  They collected trash, stopped using plastic bags, placed dustbins, and planted flowers.
Q4:  Why is smoke from traffic harmful?
Ans:  It damages the lungs, causes asthma in children, and pollutes the city's air.
Q5:  What is the central message of the lesson?
Ans:  Every individual citizen must take personal responsibility for keeping public places clean.
• Curriculum Focus: Possessive Pronouns: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs
1. This clean school is (our / ours). -> ours
2. Ali forgot his bag, but Saleem brought (his / him). -> his
► E. Forms of Verbs (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Forms)
► Letter to the Editor: Insanitary Conditions and Piles of Garbage in City
Subject: Deplorable Sanitary Conditions and Piles of Garbage

Through the esteemed columns of your widely circulated newspaper, I wish to draw the urgent attention of the Municipal Corporation and higher authorities towards the deplorable sanitary conditions prevailing in our area.

Huge piles of rotting domestic garbage and plastic bags are lying unattended along main roads and near schools. Overflowing sewer drains have turned streets into foul-smelling dirty ponds. These garbage dumps have become breeding grounds for mosquitoes and flies, causing widespread outbreaks of dengue fever and malaria among residents and young school children.

Despite repeated complaints, the municipal sanitary workers have failed to remove the heaps of waste. I earnestly appeal to the concerned municipal authorities to deploy garbage lifting trucks immediately and clean the blocked drains before epidemic diseases spread further.
I hope you will publish this letter to awaken the relevant authorities.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VII ENGLISH — UNIT 2SOCIAL ETIQUETTES AND MANNERS(2.1 Problems and Solutions (Prose))
Good social manners make everyday life pleasant and respectful.
A student named Zain wrote a letter to the newspaper column 'Ask Big Brother'.
He complained that his elder relatives were strict, but he learned the value of polite behavior.
Table Manners: Chew with mouth closed, say 'Bismillah', and do not make noise while eating.
Meeting People: Greet with 'Assalam-o-Alaikum', listen attentively, and do not interrupt.
Moral: Politeness wins hearts and reflects good family upbringing.
■  2. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Table etiquette teaches us to chew food with our mouth closed.
Use polite words like 'please' and 'thank you' when seeking assistance.
His considerate behavior won the admiration of all school staff.
Students must show sincere respect towards their teachers and parents.
The shop assistant was courteous and handed the correct change.
Wait for your turn patiently and do not interrupt talking adults.
If you bump into someone by accident, apologize immediately.
Good manners reflect the refined upbringing of a student.
Be patient while standing in a queue at the ticket counter.
A little act of kindness can brighten up an unhappy person's day.
■  3. DICTATION WORDS (20 DIFFICULT SPELLINGS WITH URDU MEANINGS)
Q1:  What was Zain's grievance in his letter to 'Ask Big Brother'?
Ans:  He felt his grandparents corrected him too often about small habits.
Q2:  List three dining table etiquettes mentioned in the lesson.
Ans:  1. Wash hands before eating. 2. Say Bismillah. 3. Chew food with your mouth closed.
Q3:  How should we behave when elders are talking?
Ans:  We should listen respectfully and never interrupt until they have finished speaking.
Q4:  Why are good manners important for students?
Ans:  Good manners earn respect from teachers, love from parents, and friendship from peers.
Q5:  What advice did Big Brother give to Zain?
Ans:  He advised Zain to understand that grandparents correct him out of love and experience.
• Curriculum Focus: Articles: A, An, The
1. He wrote ___ letter to Big Brother. -> a
3. ___ Sun rises in the east. -> The
► E. Forms of Verbs (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Forms)
► Letter to Younger Brother: Importance of Good Manners and Etiquettes

I hope you are doing well in your studies and enjoying good health. Mother mentioned in her last phone call that you sometimes lose your temper and argue with elders. I am writing this letter to share some friendly brotherly advice with you.

Good manners are the real ornaments of human character. A well-mannered student is loved and respected everywhere. Always wash your hands before eating meals, recite Bismillah, chew food quietly with your mouth closed, and never waste food on your plate.

Moreover, when parents or teachers speak, listen attentively without interrupting them. Always greet everyone with a cheerful 'Assalam-o-Alaikum'. Politeness costs nothing, but it wins everyone's heart.
I am confident you will adopt these good habits. Please write back soon.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VII ENGLISH — UNIT 3CRISIS, ACCIDENTS & CALAMITIES(3.1 Learning to Live in a Critical Situation (Prose))
Natural calamities like floods and earthquakes arrive without warning.
A brave boy named Zubair was caught in heavy monsoon floods in rural Sindh.
Water entered his village rapidly, and he helped his family evacuate to a higher embankment.
At the relief camp, Zubair volunteered to distribute food packets and clean water bottles.
Safety Rules: Never walk through rushing floodwater, boil drinking water, and stay calm.
Moral: Courage and helping others turn disasters into stories of survival.
■  2. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Eid-ul-Fitr is a joyous religious festival celebrated across Pakistan.
The school held a colorful celebration on Pakistan Resolution Day.
Celebrating national events together promotes communal harmony.
Sharing homemade sweet vermicelli on Eid is an affectionate family tradition.
Relatves exchanged gifts and enjoyed lunch at the festive family gathering.
The villagers welcomed the wedding guests with traditional hospitality.
Children wore bright new clothes and enjoyed joyful games on Eid.
Festivals strengthen the bonds of brotherhood and national unity.
Sindhi Biryani and Sajji are famous delicacies of Pakistani cuisine.
Students decorated classroom corridors with green paper buntings.
■  3. DICTATION WORDS (20 DIFFICULT SPELLINGS WITH URDU MEANINGS)
Q1:  How did Zubair react when flood water entered his village?
Ans:  He remained calm, woke up his family, and helped them carry essential documents to safety.
Q2:  What voluntary work did Zubair do at the relief camp?
Ans:  He distributed boiled water, handed out dry food rations, and looked after small children.
Q3:  Why is it dangerous to walk through moving flood water?
Ans:  Because fast-flowing currents can sweep a person away and water may hide deep open holes.
Q4:  Why must drinking water be boiled after a flood?
Ans:  To kill dangerous bacteria and prevent water-borne illnesses like cholera and diarrhea.
Q5:  What lesson does Zubair's experience teach us?
Ans:  It teaches us that staying calm, following safety rules, and helping others saves lives in emergencies.
• Curriculum Focus: First Conditional: If + Present Simple, Subject + will + V1
1. If water rises, authorities (evacuate) the village. -> will evacuate
2. If you boil water, you (avoid) cholera. -> will avoid
► E. Forms of Verbs (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Forms)
► Application to Headmaster: Leave of Absence due to Flood / Road Blockage
The Master Sahib Model High School,
Subject: Application for Three Days Leave of Absence

With profound respect, I beg to submit that due to continuous heavy monsoon rains, flood water has inundated our village and the main link road leading to the school is completely submerged and impassable.

The local administration has advised residents to remain indoors until water levels recede. Because of this emergency situation and lack of public transportation, I am unable to attend school for three days, from 22nd to 24th October, 2026.
I kindly request you to grant me leave of absence for these three days. I promise to complete all missed class assignments as soon as I return.
I shall be highly obliged for your kindness.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VII ENGLISH — UNIT 4EMPATHY WITH SPECIAL PEOPLE(4.1 The Blind Boy (Poem by Colley Cibber))
The poem is written from the perspective of an innocent blind boy.
He has never seen physical light, but he wonders what the blessings of sight are.
He feels the warm sunshine on his skin, though he cannot see the glowing sun.
He makes his own day and night: when he is awake and playing, it is day; when he sleeps, it is night.
He refuses to be pitied by sighted people because he has learned contentment.
Central Idea: Contentment of mind is true wealth; happiness comes from inner peace, not physical sight.
■  2. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
The firefighter showed extraordinary bravery while entering the blazing house.
Army helicopters rescued villagers stranded by the turbulent floodwaters.
The young girl summoned up courage and faced the menacing stray dog.
The sailor performed a heroic deed by leaping into the rough sea.
Prompt medical teams minimized casualties following the train disaster.
Keep phone numbers of local emergency rescue services on the wall.
A true patriot serves the welfare of his nation with selfless devotion.
Our brave jawans made the ultimate sacrifice to defend our frontiers.
The President conferred a medal of gallantry upon the police officer.
With relentless determination, the injured youth learned to walk again.
■  3. DICTATION WORDS (20 DIFFICULT SPELLINGS WITH URDU MEANINGS)
Q1:  How does the blind boy feel the sun without seeing it?
Ans:  He perceives the sun through its soothing physical warmth upon his face and body.
Q2:  How does the blind boy make his own day and night?
Ans:  Whenever he plays and stays awake, it is day for him; whenever he sleeps, it is night.
Q3:  Why does the blind boy refuse to be pitied?
Ans:  He refuses pity because he does not miss what he never had, and his heart is filled with patience.
Q4:  Why does the boy call himself 'a king'?
Ans:  Because his mind is contented and peaceful; his cheerfulness cannot be destroyed by his disability.
Q5:  Who wrote the poem 'The Blind Boy'?
Ans:  The poem was composed by the English poet Colley Cibber.
• Curriculum Focus: Forming Adjectives with Suffixes (-ful, -less)
► E. Forms of Verbs (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Forms)
► Dialogue: Empathy and Respect for Differently-Abled Students
Situation: Two classmates, Zain and Fahad, discussing how to support a visually impaired student named Tariq.
Zain: Fahad, I noticed a new student named Tariq in our class. He has severe vision impairment.
Fahad: Yes, I saw him walking with a white cane. We should feel very sorry and show him pity.
Zain: No, Fahad. Special persons do not want our pity; they need our empathy, friendship, and equal respect.
Fahad: What is the difference between pity and empathy?
Zain: Pity makes a person feel weak and helpless. Empathy means understanding his needs and helping him sit comfortably and share audio notes.
Fahad: That is so true! Tariq is very intelligent and sharp in oral mathematics.
Zain: Exactly. Let us guide him to the library and cafeteria so he feels completely welcome in our school.
Fahad: Wonderful idea! Let's go and shake hands with him right now.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VII ENGLISH — UNIT 5HISTORICAL PLACES OF PAKISTAN(5.1 Pakistan: Home to Ancient Civilizations (Prose))
Pakistan has a rich historical heritage dating back thousands of years.
Mohenjo-Daro (Mound of the Dead) in Larkana, Sindh, is a 5,000-year-old Indus Valley city.
It had brick-paved streets, multi-storey houses, a Great Bath, and an advanced covered drainage system.
Taxila was an ancient center of Gandhara art and Buddhist learning.
Makli Hill in Thatta is one of the world's largest ancient necropolises, famous for stone carvings.
Conclusion: We must take pride in our historical monuments and preserve them for future generations.
■  2. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Knowledge empowers young minds and drives away the darkness of ignorance.
Curious children ask clever questions to understand how machines work.
Students borrow informative science books from the municipal library.
True wisdom comes from learning lessons from life's experiences.
Astronauts build space probes to explore distant uncharted planets.
Free evening classes educate adult laborers who cannot read.
The distinguished scholar wrote authoritative textbooks on Islamic history.
Our dedicated science teacher inspires students to become doctors.
The government launched village campaigns to achieve total literacy.
Higher education is the vital foundation of modern economic progress.
■  3. DICTATION WORDS (20 DIFFICULT SPELLINGS WITH URDU MEANINGS)
Q1:  Where is Mohenjo-Daro situated and how old is it?
Ans:  It is located in Larkana district, Sindh, and is more than 5,000 years old.
Q2:  What remarkable features did the streets of Mohenjo-Daro have?
Ans:  The streets were straight, wide, paved with burnt bricks, and had covered drains.
Q3:  What was the Great Bath at Mohenjo-Daro used for?
Ans:  It was a large public pool lined with bitumen used for religious and communal bathing.
Q4:  What made ancient Taxila famous worldwide?
Ans:  Taxila was internationally famous as a center of Buddhist higher education and Gandhara stone art.
Q5:  Why is Makli Hill in Thatta globally celebrated?
Ans:  Because it is one of the world's largest necropolises, showcasing beautiful stone carvings on royal tombs.
• Curriculum Focus: Present Perfect Tense: Subject + has / have + V3
1. Archaeologists (discover) ancient terracotta seals. -> have discovered
2. Our class (visit) Mohenjo-Daro twice. -> has visited
► E. Forms of Verbs (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Forms)
► Letter to a Cousin: Describing an Educational Trip to Mohenjo-Daro

I hope you are well. Last Saturday, our school organized an educational excursion to the famous archaeological site of Mohenjo-Daro near Larkana. I am writing to share this fascinating historical experience with you.

Mohenjo-Daro is more than 5,000 years old and belongs to the ancient Indus Valley Civilization. I was astonished to see their town planning. The streets were straight and wide, lined with baked-brick houses. They even built an advanced covered drainage system and a massive public bath known as the Great Bath.
At the site museum, we saw ancient clay toys, terracotta seals, jewelry, and the famous statue of the 'Priest-King'. This visit made me feel immense pride in Pakistan's ancient cultural heritage.
You must visit this historical treasure whenever you come to Sindh. Pay my respects to uncle and aunt.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VII ENGLISH — UNIT 6MEDIA AS A SOURCE OF KNOWLEDGE(6.1 Different Newspaper News (Prose))
Newspapers are a daily window to news, sports, education, and global affairs.
Headline: A bold title that gives the most important point of the news.
Dateline: Mentions the city and date where the news happened.
Lead Paragraph: Answers the 5 Ws and 1 H: Who, What, Where, When, Why, and How.
Journalistic Rule: News must always be verified and based on objective facts, not gossip.
Conclusion: Reading daily newspapers improves English vocabulary and general knowledge.
■  2. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Regular morning jogging is vital to maintain robust physical health.
Personal hygiene rules include brushing teeth twice daily after meals.
Stagnant pools of dirty water spread malaria and waterborne disease.
Fresh seasonal fruits and pulses provide nutritious food for pupils.
Daily physical exercise keeps children active and sharpens concentration.
Cleanliness is half of faith according to the Islamic teachings.
Proper municipal sanitation prevents foul odours and insect pests.
Eight hours of sound sleep restores youthful vitality and vigor.
Drink fresh clean boiled water to avoid painful typhoid infections.
Timely vaccination is the most effective prevention against polio.
■  3. DICTATION WORDS (20 DIFFICULT SPELLINGS WITH URDU MEANINGS)
Q1:  What is the function of a headline in a newspaper?
Ans:  It catches the reader's attention and summarizes the main news in a few bold words.
Q2:  What is a dateline in a news story?
Ans:  It tells the reader the city of origin and the date on which the event took place.
Q3:  What questions does the opening lead paragraph answer?
Ans:  It answers the 5 Ws and 1 H: Who, What, Where, When, Why, and How.
Q4:  Why must journalists avoid unverified rumors?
Ans:  Because false news creates public panic, ruins reputations, and misleads citizens.
Q5:  Name two benefits of reading daily newspapers for students.
Ans:  1. It builds strong English vocabulary. 2. It keeps students updated on national and world affairs.
1. The reporter has lived in Karachi ___ 2015. -> since
2. The editor worked on the report ___ three hours. -> for

► Letter to the Editor: Unscheduled Load-Shedding during Board Exams
Subject: Frequent Load-Shedding during School Examinations

Through the columns of your highly esteemed newspaper, I wish to ventilate a serious grievance regarding the unannounced and frequent electricity load-shedding in our locality during examination days.

Our annual examinations are currently underway, and students need continuous light to study in the evenings and early mornings. Unfortunately, power outages last for eight to ten hours daily without any prior notice. Voltage fluctuations have also burnt electrical appliances and damaged computers.

Studying in sweltering heat and candle-light is severely affecting students' eyesight, concentration, and performance in papers. Despite numerous appeals, the electric power authorities have turned a deaf ear to our problems.
I earnestly request K-Electric / WAPDA authorities to exempt school examination zones from daytime load-shedding and ensure uninterrupted power supply so students can study peacefully.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS VII ENGLISH — UNIT 7LEARNING ORGANIZED APPROACH(7.1 Rafia's Wedding (Prose))
Organizing events requires advance planning, division of duties, and teamwork.
Rafia's wedding was being organized when an unexpected emergency occurred.
Her elder cousin Hassan took charge calmly and made checklists for food, seating, and lighting.
Family members were assigned specific responsibilities without confusion or arguments.
Because of systematic organization, the wedding ceremony concluded smoothly and happily.
Moral: Proper planning and cool-headed leadership turn problems into success.
■  2. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Art classes encourage children to display their natural creativity.
The village lad possessed a natural talent for singing melodious ballads.
Parents admired pupil paintings displayed at the annual school exhibition.
Reading fairy tales stimulates the fertile imagination of young kids.
Sindhi women produce exquisite Ajrak embroidery through skilled craft.
Vocational training instills useful carpentry and electrical skills.
The young writer produced an entirely original short adventure story.
Poetry is a lovely vehicle for the expression of sincere feelings.
The portrait painted by the Karachi artist was hailed as a masterpiece.
Colorful natural landscapes inspire poets to compose lyrical verse.
■  3. DICTATION WORDS (20 DIFFICULT SPELLINGS WITH URDU MEANINGS)
Q1:  What sudden problem occurred before Rafia's wedding?
Ans:  The main catering supplier delayed deliveries, threatening chaos before the arrival of wedding guests.
Q2:  How did Hassan demonstrate crisis leadership?
Ans:  He remained calm, prepared an emergency checklist, and redistributed urgent tasks among cousins.
Q3:  Why is dividing duties important in large family events?
Ans:  It prevents duplication of effort, eliminates confusion, and ensures every task is completed on time.
Q4:  How was the wedding meal handled smoothly?
Ans:  Youth volunteers managed food counters efficiently and served guests with warmth and hospitality.
Q5:  What is the main lesson taught in 'Rafia's Wedding'?
Ans:  Planning ahead, staying calm during crises, and working together leads to successful results.
• Curriculum Focus: Position of Adverbs: Frequency adverbs go before main verb
1. Hassan (always / is) punctual. -> Hassan is always punctual.
2. They (worked / skillfully) together. -> They worked skillfully together.
► E. Forms of Verbs (1st, 2nd, and 3rd Forms)
► Dialogue: Planning and Dividing Duties for School Event
Situation: Two student organizers, Hassan and Asad, making a checklist for the Annual Prize Distribution Day.
Hassan: Asad, the Annual Prize Distribution Ceremony is next Tuesday. We must get everything organized in advance.
Asad: Right! Last year there was disorder near the stage because duties were not clearly assigned.
Hassan: Let us write down an orderly checklist. Point one: Seating arrangements for guests and teachers.
Asad: I will take responsibility for decorating the main stage and checking microphones with the sound technician.
Hassan: Great. I will coordinate with the Headmaster to arrange shields and certificates in the correct order of student merit.
Asad: Who will receive chief guests at the entrance gate?
Hassan: Let us depute four smart student council members with badges and floral bouquets. Division of labour will ensure everything runs smoothly!
Asad: Agreed. Careful planning prevents last-minute panic.

■  UNIT 1: EFFECTS OF OUR ACTIONS ON THE ENVIRONMENT (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 1.1 Reading Comprehension: Can We Do Anything?
Exploring public civic duties, cleanliness, and citizen responsibility:
Pre-Reading Q1. The title of the text you are about to read is 'Can We Do Anything?' What do you think the text is about?

Ans: The text is about the alarming issue of environmental pollution in our neighbourhoods and how school students and responsible citizens can take practical steps to solve it instead of just complaining.
Pre-Reading Q2. Do you think we should do something for improving things?

Ans: Yes, absolutely. We cannot wait for others or solely depend on government agencies. Every individual citizen, young or old, has a personal moral duty to keep the surrounding environment clean and green.
Pre-Reading Q3. What is our responsibility as citizens towards bringing a good change?

Ans: Our primary responsibility is to stop littering, avoid throwing garbage on streets, plant trees, reduce smoke emissions from vehicles, dispose of waste properly, and actively raise awareness in our community.

■ POST-READING EXERCISE 4: TRUE OR FALSE STATEMENTS
Ali did not want to go to school and meet everyone.

Saleem and Ali were not able to talk about their holidays in the van.

■ POST-READING EXERCISE 6: COMPLETING REASONS FROM STORY
Reason (i): Ali excitedly got ready for school because he wanted to meet all his teachers and classmates after the long summer break.
Reason (ii): He wanted to attend the science class because he thoroughly enjoyed performing hands-on scientific experiments during the lessons.
Reason (iii): Ali sat next to Saleem because Saleem was his best friend and both shared a warm, close friendship.
Reason (iv): Some students coughed in the van because black, choking exhaust fumes from passing vehicles entered the van through the open windows.
Reason (v): The students started discussing about pollution because Miss Sana showed them thought-provoking awareness posters on environmental hazards.
Reason (vi): Miss Sana raised her hand because she used this gesture as a signal whenever she wanted pin-drop silence and complete attention.
Reason (vii): Miss Sana challenged her students' minds because she wanted them to reflect critically and take personal responsibility instead of just complaining.
Reason (viii): Ali and his friends showed posters to the people because they wanted to educate the neighbourhood youth about the severe dangers of pollution.
Reason (ix): The programme was a big success because almost all the attendees enthusiastically agreed to take practical steps to clean the locality.
Reason (x): Ali and his friends were happy because they had successfully taken a major step in the right direction toward creating a cleaner environment.
Q: Did Ali enjoy his Social Studies class? Why?

Ans: Yes, Ali enjoyed his Social Studies class immensely because his teacher, Ms. Sana Arif, constantly challenged the students' thinking, inspired active discussions, and involved them in practical social awareness campaigns rather than passive textbook lecturing.
Q: Why do you think Miss Sana showed the posters on Pollution to the class?

Ans: Miss Sana showed the posters to stimulate thoughtful discussion on environmental cleanliness, provoke critical thinking, and motivate her students to brainstorm practical solutions for their own neighbourhoods.
Q: Had the students done anything to stop pollution when Miss Sana asked them?

Ans: No, prior to Miss Sana's questioning, the students had only experienced and complained about the unattended garbage heaps and vehicle smoke, but had done nothing practical to prevent or reduce it.
Q: What did Ali and his group members do to fight against pollution?

Ans: Ali and his group members organized a comprehensive neighbourhood awareness campaign. They created educational posters, distributed informative handbills listing anti-pollution measures, delivered persuasive speeches, performed role-plays, and formulated a shared action plan with timelines for community cleaning.
Q: What do you think happened the day after the programme?

Ans: The day after the programme, the neighbourhood youth and residents gathered with brooms and bins to implement their cleaning plan. They cleared garbage heaps, sprayed stagnant water puddles, planted saplings, and presented an inspiring report to Ms. Sana in school, earning high praise from teachers and community elders.
► 1.2 Speaking: Identify a Problem and Propose a Solution
Situation: Roleplay dialogue between Saleh and Bachal on tackling stagnant water, mosquito breeding, and the spread of malaria/dengue in their locality:
Saleh: Where is Ali today? Why has he not come to school?
Bachal: He has fallen sick with severe malaria. The doctor advised complete rest.
Saleh: Oh! I am very sorry to hear that. Mosquito-borne diseases are rising dangerously.
Bachal: Yes, malaria and dengue have become severe hazards in our union council. We must do something practical about it.
Saleh: Let us start an active student campaign against mosquito breeding.
Bachal: That is a brilliant idea! How should we begin?
Saleh: First, we can educate students during morning assembly not to let water stand in broken pots, tires, or coolers.
Bachal: Yes, and we can demonstrate how spraying kerosene or larvicide on stagnant ponds suffocates mosquito larvae.
Saleh: We should also advise families to sleep under mosquito nets and install fine window mesh at home.
Bachal: Finally, let us write a joint application to our local Union Council Chairman requesting regular fumigation sprays across the entire neighbourhood.
► 1.3 Language Practice: Possessive Pronouns & Countable/Uncountable Nouns

Mansoor: Is this notebook yours, Yaqoob?
Yaqoob: No, it is not mine. My cover is green, while this one is yellow. I think it is Ali's.

► 1.4 Writing: Paragraph Writing (Pre-Writing, Focus & Model Compositions)
• Essential Pre-Writing Strategies for Paragraph Writing
1. Brainstorming: Generate a diverse cluster of ideas around the main theme.
2. Mind Mapping: Group related ideas logically under causes, effects, and solutions.
3. Formulating a Topic Sentence: State the controlling central idea clearly in the first sentence.
4. Supporting Details: Provide 4 to 6 sentences with factual reasons, examples, and descriptions.
5. Concluding Sentence: Summarize the essence with an impactful final thought.
■ EXERCISE 2: MODEL PARAGRAPHS ON POLLUTION (TOPIC SENTENCES 1 TO 5)
• Paragraph 1: Environmental Pollution in Modern Cities (Topic Sentence 1)

Environmental pollution is the single greatest hazard threatening the health of modern urban communities. Every single day, heaps of unattended domestic garbage rot in street corners, emitting sickening odours and attracting flies and disease-carrying mosquitoes. Simultaneously, millions of outdated automobiles and factories spew dense clouds of carbon smoke into the air we breathe. If civic administrations and conscious citizens do not join hands immediately to regulate waste disposal, our cities will soon turn into uninhabitable wastelands.
• Paragraph 2: The Menace of Air Pollution (Topic Sentence 2)

Air pollution causes severe respiratory ailments and long-term damage to the quality of human life. In crowded towns, toxic vehicle exhaust fumes and industrial smoke fill the atmosphere with harmful carbon monoxide and particulate matter. Schoolchildren and elderly citizens constantly suffer from chronic coughing, asthma attacks, and eye irritation. Planting thousands of neem and peepal trees alongside roads is the most natural and cost-effective remedy to purify our urban atmosphere.
• Paragraph 3: Contamination of Drinking Water (Topic Sentence 3)

Water pollution is a grave crisis that deprives millions of families of safe drinking water. When chemical effluents from factories and untreated municipal sewage are poured directly into freshwater canals and rivers, marine life is destroyed and underground aquifers are poisoned. Drinking this contaminated water triggers deadly waterborne diseases such as cholera, typhoid, and hepatitis. The government must establish modern sewage treatment plants and strictly penalize industrial polluters.
• Paragraph 4: Noise Pollution on Busy Roads (Topic Sentence 4)

Excessive noise pollution on public roads is an overlooked civic menace that damages physical and mental peace. Loud power horns, modified silencers on motorbikes, and non-stop blaring of pressure horns create unbearable acoustic chaos in our cities. Medical research shows that persistent traffic noise leads to hearing impairment, heightened blood pressure, chronic sleep disorders, and severe stress among students. Traffic police must enforce strict bans against pressure horns and fine reckless drivers immediately.
• Paragraph 5: The Role of Students in Environmental Protection (Topic Sentence 5)

School students possess immense energy and enthusiasm to spearhead positive environmental change in Pakistan. Instead of adopting a passive mindset and merely complaining about filthy streets, young learners can launch active social campaigns in their localities. They can organize litter-picking drives, distribute awareness handbills, discourage the burning of leaves and plastic, and plant greenery in open spaces. When youth demonstrate civic responsibility, the entire community is inspired to protect nature.
■ EXERCISE 3: MODEL PARAGRAPH ON PUBLIC PLAYGROUNDS
Model Composition: The Need and Benefits of Public Playgrounds

Public playgrounds and sports parks are indispensable for the holistic physical, mental, and social development of young children. In today's dense urban neighbourhoods, multi-storey apartment blocks have swallowed open grounds, confining youngsters to sedentary indoor habits and addictive smartphone screens. Well-maintained neighbourhood playgrounds provide safe spaces where children can run, play cricket, football, and interact with peers in the fresh open air. Regular outdoor sports build strong bones, improve cardiovascular stamina, and teach essential life values such as teamwork, fair play, and resilience in the face of defeat. Both local municipal authorities and community elders must ensure that public playgrounds are protected from land grabbers, kept completely free of litter and broken glass, and enriched with green grass and sturdy athletic equipment for future generations.
► 1.5 Study Skills: Free-Writing Technique to Build Fluency
• Study Skills Technique: Free-Writing to Overcome Writer's Block
• Purpose: Free-writing is a proven educational strategy to conquer writer's block and develop natural, uninterrupted written fluency.
• Golden Rule: Set a timer for 10 minutes. Put pen to paper and write non-stop without pausing to check spelling, grammar, or punctuation.
• Flow of Ideas: Let your thoughts flow directly onto the page. If you get stuck on a word, write 'and then' or repeat the last thought until ideas resume.
• Post-Writing Editing: Once the timer rings, read your draft, circle your best ideas, correct errors, and polish it into a coherent paragraph.
Ten-Minute Free-Writing Sample on 'A Clean and Green Pakistan':

I close my eyes and imagine what my city would look like if every citizen planted just one shady tree outside their gate. It would be cool and peaceful and birds would sing in the branches early in the morning instead of the loud screeching horns of buses and vans. Cleanliness is not just a government duty; it begins right at our own doorstep. If I stop throwing juice boxes from moving cars, my friend will see me and stop doing it too. We could organize weekend teams of boys and girls with reusable canvas bags to clear the plastic bottles from our football field. When an area is neat and green, people naturally feel happier and healthier. A clean neighbourhood creates a proud nation where everyone breathes fresh air with dignity and joy.
► 1.6 Fun Time: Creative Slogans & Visual Anti-Pollution Posters
• Catchy Environmental Slogans for School Banners
1. 'Plant a Tree Today, Breathe Clean Air Tomorrow!'
2. 'Be Part of the Solution, Not Part of the Pollution!'
3. 'Cleanliness is Half of Faith — Keep Our Streets Clean and Safe!'
4. 'Drop Trash in the Bin, Help Your City Win!'
5. 'Cut the Horns, Save the Peace — Let the Road Noise Cease!'
• Top Banner: 'GREEN SINDH, CLEAN SINDH' in bold green lettering.
• Visual Contrast: Split the poster into two halves:
- Left Half (The Dark Reality): Smoke-belching factories, dirty heaps of plastic bags, dry stumps, coughing children.
- Right Half (The Clean Vision): Lush green trees, solar energy panels, crystal-clear flowing streams, children smiling on playground swings.
• Bottom Call to Action: 'Small Daily Steps Create Big Miracles. Join the Youth Cleanliness Campaign!'
