► 7.4 Writing: An Essay on 'The Indispensable Role of Women in Nation Building'
• Multi-Paragraph Essay: The Indispensable Role of Women in Nation Building

Women constitute nearly half of the world's population and represent the vital cornerstone of societal progress. In the words of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, 'No nation can rise to the height of glory unless its women are side by side with men.' From managing households to pioneering scientific breakthroughs, women perform diverse and indispensable roles that sustain family life and advance national prosperity.
II. The Domestic and Moral Pillar:

Within the domestic sphere, women serve as mothers, daughters, and wives, forming the emotional and moral backbone of society. As primary caregivers, mothers nurture young minds, instill ethical values, and ensure the physical and psychological well-being of future generations. This unpaid domestic labour, though frequently overlooked, provides the stability upon which all economic activity rests.
III. Economic, Professional, and Agricultural Leadership:

Beyond the home, modern Pakistani women excel across diverse professional frontiers. In rural areas, women drive agricultural productivity by harvesting crops, tending livestock, and sustaining rural commerce. In urban sectors, female professionals shine as compassionate doctors, innovative software engineers, visionary entrepreneurs, dedicated teachers, and fearless pilots, contributing significantly to national GDP.

In conclusion, the empowerment and education of women are fundamental prerequisites for a prosperous Pakistan. When women are equipped with knowledge, respect, and equal opportunities, entire communities thrive. Empowering women is not merely a matter of social justice; it is the most effective investment in our nation's sustainable future.

Q1:  What is meant by the phrase 'Dignity of Work'?
Ans:  It means having respect for all kinds of honest work, whether done with hands or with the mind.
Q2:  How did the Holy Prophet (P.B.U.H) show respect for manual labor?
Ans:  He mended his own shoes, patched his clothes, swept his house, and helped his companions build the mosque.
Q3:  Give an example of how Hazrat Umar (R.A) practiced dignity of work.
Ans:  Hazrat Umar (R.A) carried a heavy bag of flour on his own back at night to feed starving children.
Q4:  Why do developed nations prosper?
Ans:  Developed nations prosper because they respect all workers equally and no honest job is looked down upon.
Q5:  What happens when people feel ashamed of manual work?
Ans:  They become lazy, dependent on others, and their country faces poverty and unemployment.
► Topic A: Three Forms of Common Irregular Verbs
• Topic B: Simple and Compound Sentences
1. He was tired. He continued to work. -> He was tired, but he continued to work.
2. The boy worked hard. He passed the exam. -> The boy worked hard, so he passed the exam.
• Topic C: Change into Negative & Interrogative
-> Negative: He did not mend his shoes.
-> Interrogative: Did he mend his shoes?
-> Negative: They do not respect honest workers.
-> Interrogative: Do they respect honest workers?
► Formal Email: Requesting Books for School Library
Subject: Request for New Books on Great Personalities
I am writing this email on behalf of the students of Class X. Our school library needs new books on
the life of the Holy Prophet (P.B.U.H) and our national heroes, emphasizing the dignity of manual labor.
These books will inspire students to work hard and develop good character.
We kindly request you to approve the purchase of these books for the library.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 3PRACTICING POSITIVE WORK ETHICS(3.1 King Bruce and the Spider (Poem by Eliza Cook))
King Robert Bruce of Scotland fought six battles for his country but was defeated each time.
He was hiding in a dark cave, feeling hopeless and ready to give up.
He noticed a tiny spider trying to climb up a slippery beam to weave its web.
The spider failed nine times, but it did not give up.
On the tenth attempt, the spider reached the top successfully.
Inspired by the spider, King Bruce gathered his men, fought again, and won his kingdom.
Central Idea: Never lose hope; continuous effort and perseverance always bring success.
• Poem: 'King Bruce and the Spider' by Eliza Cook
"Up, up it ran, not a second it stayed, / To complain of its easy fall,
And softly the spider began to thread / Its way to the top of the wall."
Reference: These lines are taken from the poem 'King Bruce and the Spider', written by Eliza Cook.
Context: The spider had fallen nine times, but it refused to give up.
Simple Explanation: The spider showed great patience and courage. Instead of crying over failures, it tried again and achieved its goal. This taught King Bruce the value of hard work.
■  3. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Her heart was filled with deep grief after the tragic accident.
We must never give way to despair even in the darkest hours.
If you persevere through hard times, success will surely follow.
The climber clung firmly to the rocky edge of the mountain.
The mountain path was narrow and slippery after heavy rain.
Sacrificing personal comfort for others is a truly noble deed.
The soldiers defended their homeland with tremendous courage.
Hardworking students can easily overcome difficult study topics.
Pakistan gained a historic victory in the world cricket tournament.
Patience is a great virtue that helps us face life's trials.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
Q1:  Why was King Robert Bruce feeling sad and hopeless?
Ans:  He was defeated six times by the English army and had failed to free his motherland Scotland.
Q2:  What was the tiny spider trying to do in the cave?
Ans:  The spider was trying to reach a beam on the ceiling to spin its web.
Q3:  How many times did the spider fail before succeeding?
Ans:  The spider failed nine times, but succeeded on the tenth attempt.
Q4:  What lesson did King Bruce learn from the spider?
Ans:  He learned that failure is not the end; with patience and repeated effort, success is guaranteed.
Q5:  What did King Bruce do after watching the spider?
Ans:  He collected his army once again, fought bravely, and liberated his country.
1. King Bruce was ___ brave king. -> King Bruce was a brave king.
2. He hid inside ___ dark cave. -> He hid inside a dark cave.
3. ___ spider tried ten times. -> The spider tried ten times.
4. He made ___ honest effort. -> He made an honest effort.
• Topic B: Simple Past vs Past Continuous Tense
1. King Bruce (lie) on the ground. -> King Bruce was lying on the ground.
2. Suddenly he (see) a spider. -> Suddenly he saw a spider.
3. The soldiers (fight) with courage. -> The soldiers fought with courage.
► Summary of 'King Bruce and the Spider'

King Robert Bruce was the ruler of Scotland. He fought six wars to save his people, but was defeated. He hid in a cave and lost all hope. There, he saw a spider trying to reach a beam to make its web. The spider fell down nine times, but did not lose courage. On the tenth try, it reached the top. Seeing this, the King gathered his courage. He attacked his enemies again and freed Scotland. Moral: Try, try again until you succeed.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 4MEDIA FOR INFORMATION AND REFLECTION(4.1 Social Media (Prose))
Social media means computer apps and websites that let people share ideas and information.
Examples of social media include WhatsApp, YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram.
Advantages: Students can study online, find information quickly, and stay in touch with relatives.
Disadvantages: Spending too much time on mobile phones hurts eyes, wastes time, and spreads fake news.
Conclusion: Students should use social media only for positive educational purposes with time limits.
Social media provides a vast network for connecting people worldwide.
The internet is a powerful platform for sharing academic knowledge.
Excessive gaming leads to screen addiction among school children.
We must verify news before sharing it to avoid spreading fake rumors.
Excessive use of mobile phones damages eyesight and causes headaches.
Face-to-face interaction is very important for healthy family life.
Schools should formulate strict rules to prevent cyberbullying.
Online educational tutorials are highly beneficial for board students.
Every user must be responsible while posting comments on the web.
Teachers created public awareness regarding digital safety.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
Ans:  Social media includes online websites and apps that allow people to communicate and share content instantly.
Q2:  State two major benefits of social media for students.
Ans:  1. Students can watch educational video lectures. 2. They can share study notes with classmates.
Q3:  What are the harmful effects of excessive social media use?
Ans:  It causes eye weakness, sleep deprivation, lack of focus on studies, and physical laziness.
Q4:  How can students protect their privacy online?
Ans:  They should never share passwords or personal home details with unknown strangers on the internet.
Q5:  What role should parents play regarding internet use?
Ans:  Parents should fix daily time limits for screen time and guide children to use the internet safely.
• Topic A: Active and Passive Voice (Future Tense)
Formula: Object + will be + V3 + by + Subject
1. Students will use social media for learning. -> Social media will be used by students for learning.
2. The teacher will check the online homework. -> The online homework will be checked by the teacher.
3. Hackers will steal weak passwords. -> Weak passwords will be stolen by hackers.
• Topic B: Prepositions of Position and Instrument
1. We connect with people ___ social media. -> on
2. Students watch video lectures ___ YouTube. -> on
3. She sent the message ___ WhatsApp. -> through
4. Do not look at screens ___ the dark. -> in
► Paragraph: Uses and Abuses of Social Media

Social media has completely changed modern communication. It has both advantages and disadvantages. On the positive side, students can learn English, science, and math through online tutorials. It also helps people connect with family living abroad. However, excessive use of mobile phones has serious disadvantages. Students waste precious study hours playing games or scrolling videos. It weakens eyesight and prevents outdoor exercise. Therefore, students must use social media wisely and in moderation.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 5RESPECTING SELF AND OTHERS(5.1 A Bad Dream (Prose))
A boy had bad habits of being rude, shouting at his sister, and teasing classmates.
He thought he was superior to everyone and refused to respect others.
One night, he saw a scary nightmare where he was trapped in a dark forest.
In the dream, wild beasts chased him, and all the people he had insulted refused to help him.
He woke up sweating and frightened, and realized that bad behavior leads to loneliness.
He changed his character, asked forgiveness from his family, and became a respectful person.
The bad accident seemed like a terrifying nightmare to the boy.
We should never use rude words while talking to our elders.
No person is superior to another on the basis of wealth or race.
The small child was terrified when he heard the loud thunder.
He soon realized his mistake and offered an apology.
Take a few quiet moments to reflect on your daily conduct.
Arrogance always leads to a person's ultimate downfall.
A humble attitude earns respect and love in society.
A positive attitude helps students achieve top marks in exams.
Islam teaches us to forgive others when they admit their faults.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
Q1:  What bad habits did the boy have at the beginning of the story?
Ans:  He was arrogant, rude to his younger sister, and constantly made fun of his school friends.
Q2:  What nightmare did the boy see in his sleep?
Ans:  He dreamed he was lost in a dark jungle chased by wild beasts, but nobody came to rescue him.
Q3:  Why did no one help the boy in his dream?
Ans:  Because he had always hurt their feelings and treated them with disrespect in real life.
Q4:  What was the boy's reaction when he woke up?
Ans:  He was sweating and trembling with fear. He immediately hugged his mother and apologized.
Q5:  What moral lesson does the story teach us?
Ans:  If you want others to respect you, you must first respect them.
• Topic: Modal Verbs (Can, Could, Must, Should)
1. You (should / can) not tease younger children. -> You should not tease younger children.
2. We (must / may) obey traffic rules. -> We must obey traffic rules.
3. (Can / May) I help you carry these heavy books? -> May I help you carry these heavy books?
► Letter to the Editor: Insanitary Conditions in the Area
Subject: Poor Sanitary Conditions in Nishtar Road Area
Through the columns of your esteemed newspaper, I wish to draw the attention of the authorities
towards the heaps of garbage and broken sewerage pipes in our locality. The dirty water has accumulated
in the streets, creating a breeding ground for mosquitoes and flies. Residents, especially school children,
are suffering from malaria and dengue.
I request the municipal authorities to clear the garbage immediately.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 6CHARACTER BUILDING(6.1 Speak Gently (Poem by David Bates))
The poet tells us to speak gently to all people at all times.
Harsh words break hearts and cause sadness that lasts forever.
Speak gently to young children so they learn love and good manners.
Speak gently to old people whose lives are ending and who need comforting words.
Speak softly to the poor and needy without hurting their self-respect.
Central Idea: A kind word costs nothing, but it wins hearts in this world and earns reward in the Hereafter.
"Speak gently!—'tis a little thing / Dropped in the heart's deep well;
The good, the joy, which it may bring, / Eternity shall tell."
Reference: These lines are taken from the poem 'Speak Gently', written by David Bates.
Context: The poet highlights the lasting power of soft and loving speech.
Simple Explanation: Speaking softly takes very little effort, but its good results stay in a person's heart forever. God rewards kind speech in eternity.
■  3. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Speak gently so that you do not hurt anyone's feelings.
Harsh words break hearts and destroy long-lasting friendships.
Kind and loving deeds remain remembered throughout eternity.
A true friend shares our joy and comforts us in sorrow.
The brave patient endured the painful treatment without complaining.
Youth and worldly riches are fleeting and do not last forever.
Time gradually heals the deepest wounds of human grief.
Kind words banish anger and restore harmony among people.
The kind mother looked at her newborn baby with tender affection.
The children whispered quietly so they would not disturb the class.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
Q1:  Why does the poet advise us to 'Speak Gently'?
Ans:  Because gentle words rule hearts through love, whereas harsh words cause pain and hatred.
Q2:  Why should we speak gently to little children?
Ans:  Little children have tender hearts. Kind words teach them love, while scolding makes them timid and bitter.
Q3:  Why must we speak softly to the aged?
Ans:  Old people have experienced many hardships. They need affection, care, and peaceful words in their final days.
Q4:  What does the poet say about speaking to the poor?
Ans:  The poet says the poor already carry heavy burdens of poverty; we must never hurt them with arrogant speech.
Q5:  What reward does gentle speech bring in eternity?
Ans:  God is pleased with kind people and grants them eternal peace and blessing in the Hereafter.
1. The teacher said, "Speak gently to everyone."
-> The teacher advised the students to speak gently to everyone.
2. He said to me, "Do not use harsh words."
-> He forbade me to use harsh words.
► Expository Essay: Importance of Good Manners

Good manners are the foundation of a peaceful civilized society. A well-mannered person speaks politely, respects elders, and helps the weak. Saying simple words like 'Please', 'Thank You', and 'Sorry' costs nothing, but creates harmony among people. In contrast, rudeness and harsh language produce enemies and destroy relationships. Our Holy Prophet (P.B.U.H) was the best example of polite manners and gentle speech. As students, we should always practice kindness in our speech with teachers, parents, and friends.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 7PRAISING NATURE(7.1 My Travel Diary: Journey to the Gorakh Hills Station (Prose))
Gorakh Hill is a famous hill station located in the Kirthar Mountains in Dadu district, Sindh.
It is situated at a height of 5,688 feet above sea level.
Due to its cool and pleasant climate, it is called the 'Murree of Sindh'.
Visitors travel in four-wheel drive 4x4 jeeps through winding mountain roads.
The top offers stunning views of golden sunsets, starry night skies, and peaceful mountain scenery.
Mountaineers face breathing difficulty at high altitudes due to thin air.
چوٹی / پہاڑ کا سب سے اونچا مقام
The climbers celebrated joyfully when they reached the summit of K2.
The northern valleys of Pakistan are world-famous for scenic beauty.
The winding mountain road leads travellers safely through the hills.
After ten hours of journey, the passenger bus arrived at its destination.
The majestic snowy peaks of Nanga Parbat looked breathtaking at dawn.
Green pine trees and cold streams decorate the beautiful Kaghan valley.
Melting glaciers provide fresh water to our rivers throughout summer.
Trekking across the northern passes was an exciting adventure for students.
The sunset view over Saif-ul-Malook lake was breathtaking.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
ہڈیوں کو جما دینے والی سردی
الاؤ / کھلے میں جلائی گئی آگ
Q1:  Where is Gorakh Hill Station located?
Ans:  It is located in the Kirthar Mountain Range, in Dadu district, Sindh, at an altitude of 5,688 feet.
Q2:  Why is Gorakh Hill called the 'Murree of Sindh'?
Ans:  Because it enjoys cool weather and occasional snowfall in winter, while the rest of Sindh experiences hot temperatures.
Q3:  Why are 4x4 jeeps needed to reach the summit?
Ans:  Because the road from Wahi Pandi to Gorakh Hill is very steep, rugged, and winding.
Q4:  What natural attractions do tourists enjoy at Gorakh Hill?
Ans:  Tourists enjoy breathtaking sunsets, panoramic mountain views, cool breezes, and night stargazing.
Q5:  What should tourists carry when visiting Gorakh Hill?
Ans:  They should carry warm jackets, drinking water, first-aid medicine, and good walking shoes.
• Topic A: Prepositions of Direction and Movement
2. The 4x4 jeep drove ___ the steep mountain. -> up
3. The road passes ___ deep valleys. -> through
4. Tourists walked ___ the vast plateau. -> across
Formula: If + had + V3, Subject + would have + V3
1. If we had taken warm jackets, we would not have felt cold.
2. If the jeep had not broken down, they would have reached before sunset.
► Descriptive Essay: A Trip to a Hill Station

Visiting a hill station is a refreshing experience away from city noise and pollution. Last month, we visited Gorakh Hill Station in Sindh. The mountain air was crisp and cool. Traveling in a four-wheel jeep along the winding hills was adventurous and thrilling. When we reached the summit in the evening, the setting sun turned the sky into golden red. At night, the sky was filled with thousands of bright stars. This wonderful trip helped us appreciate the majestic natural beauty created by Almighty God.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 8CIVIC SENSE AND SAFETY MEASURES(8.1 Safety Measures That Can Save Your Life (Prose))
Civic sense means being responsible and following safety rules for ourselves and others.
Electrical Safety: Never touch live wires or switches with wet hands; turn off appliances when not in use.
Fire Safety: If your clothes catch fire, remember to 'Stop, Drop, and Roll' on the ground.
Road Safety: Always cross the road on zebra crossings and follow traffic light signals.
First Aid: Keep an emergency first-aid kit at home with bandages, antiseptics, and burn lotion.
Throwing trash into bins is an essential part of good civic sense.
Wearing a helmet while riding a motorcycle is a necessary precaution.
Call the fire brigade immediately in case of a burning emergency.
The brave firefighters worked hard to extinguish the raging factory fire.
Every school laboratory should have a well-equipped first-aid box.
Residents were evacuated safely before the rising flood waters reached homes.
Earthquakes and floods are natural disasters that demand prompt relief work.
Rescue teams arrived swiftly and saved all trapped passengers.
Naked electric wires present a severe hazard during heavy monsoon rains.
Always observe road safety rules while crossing busy avenues.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
Q1:  What is meant by 'Civic Sense'?
Ans:  Civic sense means following social rules, keeping the city clean, and showing care for the safety of fellow citizens.
Q2:  What should you do if your clothes catch fire?
Ans:  Never run. Remember to: 1. Stop immediately. 2. Drop to the ground. 3. Roll back and forth until the flames are out.
Q3:  State two electrical safety precautions inside the house.
Ans:  1. Never touch switches or wires with wet hands. 2. Do not overload one power socket with multiple plugs.
Q4:  How should pedestrians cross a busy road safely?
Ans:  They should use zebra crossings or pedestrian bridges, and look right, left, and right again before crossing.
Q5:  What essential items should be present in a first-aid box?
Ans:  Antiseptic liquid (Dettol), cotton wool, sterile bandages, burn cream, and medical scissors.
• Topic A: Relative Pronouns (Who, Which, That, Whose)
1. This is the doctor. He treated the burn patient. -> This is the doctor who treated the burn patient.
2. The wire was loose. It caused the short circuit. -> The wire which was loose caused the short circuit.
• Topic B: Direct and Indirect Speech (Commands and Requests)
1. The officer said to him, "Turn off the gas cylinder!"
-> The officer ordered him to turn off the gas cylinder.
2. The doctor said to the patient, "Take your medicine on time."
-> The doctor advised the patient to take his medicine on time.
3. Ali said to his brother, "Please give me the first-aid kit."
-> Ali requested his brother to give him the first-aid kit.
► Paragraph: Road Safety is Everyone's Responsibility

Road accidents take thousands of innocent human lives every year. Most accidents happen because of over-speeding, jumping red traffic signals, and using mobile phones while driving. Both drivers and pedestrians must follow traffic rules strictly. Motorcyclists must wear safety helmets, and car drivers must wear seatbelts. Pedestrians must only cross at zebra crossings. By developing road civic sense, we can protect our lives and make our roads safe.

Note: This section consists of 20 Multiple Choice Questions. All questions are compulsory. (1 Mark each)

Note: Answer any FIVE (5) of the following questions in 2 to 3 simple sentences. (4 Marks each)
Q1. Why did the poet Louis I. Newman climb the church steeple, and what message did God give him?
Model Answer: He climbed the highest steeple believing he would hear God from above. God replied: 'Go down again; I dwell among the people,' teaching that serving humanity is true worship of God.
Q2. What historic vision did Allama Iqbal present in his Allahabad Address of 1930?
Model Answer: Allama Iqbal demanded an autonomous consolidated North-West Indian Muslim state, declaring that Islam is a complete cultural, social, and political code of life for Indian Muslims.
Q3. What did Quaid-e-Azam advise regarding religious freedom in his 11th August 1947 inaugural speech?
Model Answer: He declared that citizens of Pakistan are completely free to go to their temples, mosques, or places of worship. The State makes no discrimination based on religion, caste, or creed.
Q4. Describe two historical examples proving the dignity of manual work in Islam.
Model Answer: Hazrat Umar (R.A) walked while his slave rode the camel into Jerusalem, and Hazrat Fatima (R.A) ground grain with her own hands until blisters formed on her palms.
Q5. What key role did King Faisal play in uniting Muslim nations worldwide?
Model Answer: King Faisal organized the historic Second Islamic Summit Conference at Lahore in 1974, generously donated oil wealth to poor Islamic states, and strongly defended Arab rights.
Q6. According to David Bates in 'Speak Gently', why must we speak softly to little children and the aged?
Model Answer: We should speak gently to children because childhood is tender and short, and to the aged because they are tired, lonely, and departing soon from this earthly life.
Q7. According to Ralph Waldo Emerson, what makes a nation truly strong and invincible?
Model Answer: Not gold, arms, or wealth, but brave and honest citizens who stand firm and suffer for truth and honour make a nation's pillars deep and lift them to the sky.
Q8. What safety rules should be followed during an earthquake and heavy urban floods?
Model Answer: During earthquakes, practice 'Drop, Cover, and Hold On' under a sturdy table. In floods, switch off main electric circuit breakers and never walk or drive through moving water.
► Part-II: Grammar & Language in Use (Do as Directed) — [15 Marks]
Note: Attempt the following grammar questions according to the instructions in brackets. (1 Mark each)
1. The students have completed the science project. [Change into Passive Voice]   → Solution: The science project has been completed by the students.
2. We should respect our national heroes. [Change into Passive Voice]   → Solution: Our national heroes should be respected by us.
3. The teacher said to the students, 'Work hard for your examinations.' [Change into Indirect Speech]   → Solution: The teacher advised the students to work hard for their examinations.
4. Ali said, 'I have bought a new bicycle today.' [Change into Indirect Speech]   → Solution: Ali said that he had bought a new bicycle that day.
5. He is ___ M.A. in English literature. [Insert suitable Article (a, an, the)]   → Solution: He is an M.A. in English literature.
6. The cat hid ___ the wooden table. [Insert suitable Preposition (under, into, on)]   → Solution: The cat hid under the wooden table.
7. They have been living in Karachi ___ ten years. [Insert suitable Preposition (since / for)]   → Solution: They have been living in Karachi for ten years.
8. If you work hard, you (pass) the examination. [Complete with First Conditional]   → Solution: If you work hard, you will pass the examination.
9. If I had money, I (help) the poor people. [Complete with Second Conditional]   → Solution: If I had money, I would help the poor people.
10. He did not attend school yesterday. [Change into Affirmative Sentence]   → Solution: He attended school yesterday. (or: He was absent yesterday.)
11. Iron is the (useful) of all metals. [Use correct Degree of Adjective]   → Solution: Iron is the most useful of all metals.
12. Change the adjective 'brave' into an Abstract Noun: [Form Noun]   → Solution: Bravery
13. Change the noun 'success' into an Adjective: [Form Adjective]   → Solution: Successful
14. Punctuate the sentence: quaid e azam said work work and work [Punctuate and Capitalize]   → Solution: Quaid-e-Azam said, 'Work, work and work.'
15. The train had left before he (reach) the station. [Use correct form of verb]   → Solution: The train had left before he reached the station.
► Part-III: Translation into Urdu / Sindhi — [5 Marks]

Q. Translate the following English passage into Urdu:"Islam lays great stress on the dignity of labour. All prophets of Allah worked with their own hands to earn a livelihood. Our Holy Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H) never looked down upon any work. He mended his own shoes, washed his own clothes, and swept his home. Honest hard work brings honour and self-respect in society."

Model Answer (Alternative Note — 'Dignity of Work'): Islam lays tremendous emphasis on the dignity of labour and manual work. All holy prophets earned their living through honest hard work. The Holy Prophet Muhammad (P.B.U.H) never felt shy of doing physical work, mending his shoes, and helping in chores. Respecting manual labour builds honest, dignified, and prosperous societies.
► Q1. Detailed Composition / Essay Writing — [12 Marks]
Write a comprehensive essay of 120 to 150 words on ANY ONE of the following top-guess topics:
1. Street Crimes in Karachi: Causes and Remedies
2. Traffic Hazards and Fatal Road Accidents in Karachi
3. Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah: My Ideal Hero
4. Role of Women in National Development
► Complete Model Essay: Street Crimes in Karachi: Causes and Remedies

Street crime has become one of the most alarming and disturbing problems in Karachi today. Everyday, innocent citizens are robbed of their mobile phones, cash, motorcycles, and precious belongings at gunpoint in broad daylight. Unfortunately, many young individuals lose their precious lives simply for resisting armed bandits on busy roads and intersections.

The root causes of this rampant lawlessness include high youth unemployment, skyrocketing inflation, poverty, easy availability of illegal weapons, and widespread drug addiction. When educated youth cannot find honest employment, frustration drives some toward unlawful activities. Furthermore, lack of adequate police patrolling and non-functional streetlights provide safe havens for criminals.

To curb this menace, the government must install functional CCTV security cameras across all major roads and market areas. Police patrols and quick response squads should be increased, especially during evening hours. Above all, illegal weapons must be seized and fast-track courts should award strict punishment to criminals so that the citizens of Karachi can live in peace and safety.
► Q2. Letter to the Editor OR Application to Principal — [10 Marks]
► Model Letter to the Editor: Acute Water Shortage and Contaminated Supply in Karachi
Subject: Acute Water Crisis and Supply of Contaminated Water in Karachi

Through the esteemed columns of your widely circulated daily, I wish to draw the urgent attention of the Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation (KWSC) and higher provincial authorities towards the severe water crisis in our locality.

For the past several weeks, our taps have run completely dry. Poor residents are forced to purchase costly private commercial water tankers, which they can hardly afford. To make matters worse, whenever tap water is released, it is heavily contaminated with muddy sewage water and emits a foul odor. Drinking this impure water has triggered water-borne diseases like diarrhea, typhoid, and stomach infections among children and elders.

Clean drinking water is a fundamental constitutional right of every citizen. I appeal to the concerned municipal authorities to repair leaking pipelines immediately, take strict action against illegal water hydrants, and ensure equitable, clean piped water supply to all residential areas.
I hope this public issue will receive prompt publication in your esteemed paper.
► Q3. Summary of Poem / Central Idea — [8 Marks]
Write a concise summary of ANY ONE of the following poems:(1) Speak Gently   (2) A Nation's Strength   (3) Beautiful Hands
► Model Summary: Speak Gently (By David Bates)
The poem 'Speak Gently' is composed by the famous American poet David Bates.
The poet advises us to always speak with polite, soft, and gentle words rather than harsh or angry tones.
We must speak gently to little children because their young hearts are tender and easily hurt.
We must also speak with deep compassion to the elderly whose tired earthly days are few.
Central Idea: Harsh speech causes bitterness and destroys love, whereas gentleness wins human hearts, brings inner peace, and earns divine blessing.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given at the end:Discipline is the foundation of every successful human society. In simple terms, discipline means obeying rules, respecting laws, and acting in an orderly manner. Without discipline, civilization would degenerate into chaos and confusion. In nature, we observe perfect discipline: the sun rises and sets at precise moments, the seasons change in predictable harmony, and even tiny ants march together in strict order. In school life, discipline teaches students punctuality, focus, and moral self-control. On the battlefield, disciplined soldiers triumph against much larger enemy forces. A nation whose citizens respect queue lines, obey traffic signals, and pay honest taxes progresses rapidly. Hence, self-discipline is the true key to individual greatness and national prosperity.
(1) What does discipline mean in simple words?  →  Ans: Discipline means obeying rules, respecting established laws, and behaving in an orderly, self-controlled manner.
(2) How does nature demonstrate the law of discipline?  →  Ans: In nature, the sun, moon, and seasons operate in perfect, punctual harmony, and ants work together in strict orderly lines.
(3) How does discipline benefit school students?  →  Ans: It teaches students punctuality, moral self-control, mental focus, and prepares them for successful adult careers.
(4) Suggest a suitable title for the passage.  →  Ans: Title: 'The Importance of Discipline in Life'

■  UNIT 1: CONTRIBUTIONS OF NOTABLE LEADERS (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 1.1 Reading Comprehension: The Voice of God (Poem by Louis I. Newman) & The Wise Caliph (Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid)
Pre-Reading Q1. Where can true divine guidance and the voice of God be discovered?

Ans: As the poet Louis I. Newman realized, God does not dwell high in remote stone steeples away from creation; rather, His divine voice and pleasure are found down among suffering, humble human beings who need love and care.
Pre-Reading Q2. What qualities made Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid a legendary model of judicial wisdom?
Ans: Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid was renowned for his astute discernment, impartiality, deep understanding of human psychology, and commitment to delivering absolute justice to every citizen.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN UNIT TABLE
A tall, pointed tower on top of a religious building
A supreme civil and religious Muslim ruler / head of the Islamic state
A sharp disagreement, argument, or legal conflict between parties
A person who is physically disabled or unable to walk normally
Having or showing good judgment and acute insight
Treating all rivals or disputants equally; fair and just
A leather lash used for driving horses or administering punishment
A judge presiding in an Islamic court of law
In 'The Voice of God', the poet climbed the highest steeple to hear God speak.
God commanded the poet to remain on top of the steeple forever.
False (F) — God declared: 'Go down again; I dwell among the people.'
The rich man and the beggar in 'The Wise Caliph' disputed the ownership of a fine horse.
The horse showed affection and joy when the lame beggar touched it in the stable.
False (F) — The horse winced and turned away from the beggar, but neighed happily when the rich man stroked it.
Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid punished the liar and forgave him after he repented.
MCQ 1. Who wrote the short, philosophical poem 'The Voice of God'?  • a. Louis I. Newman  • b. Eliza Cook  • c. William Wordsworth  • d. David Bates
MCQ 2. What did God command the poet when he climbed the steeple?  • a. Build a taller tower  • b. 'Go down again; I dwell among the people'  • c. Read all books  • d. Ring the bell
Ans: b. 'Go down again; I dwell among the people'

MCQ 3. How did Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid definitively identify the true owner of the horse?  • a. By checking government registration papers  • b. By observing the horse's natural physical reaction to both claimants in the stable  • c. By tossing a gold coin  • d. By asking the crowd
Ans: b. By observing the horse's natural physical reaction to both claimants in the stable

MCQ 4. What moral virtue does the case of the Wise Caliph illustrate?  • a. Astute judicial investigation and mercy towards a repentant wrongdoer  • b. Cruelty  • c. Hasty judgments  • d. Favoring the rich
Ans: a. Astute judicial investigation and mercy towards a repentant wrongdoer
Q1. What is the central spiritual moral of the poem 'The Voice of God'?

Ans: The poem conveys that spiritual communion with God cannot be achieved by isolating oneself from humanity in lofty architectural monuments. True service to the Creator requires descending to the community, helping the needy, comforting the sick, and living among our fellow human beings.
Q2. Describe the dispute brought before Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid between the rich man and the beggar.

Ans: A well-dressed rich man gave a ride on his magnificent horse to a lame beggar who begged for a lift into Baghdad. Upon reaching the city, the ungrateful beggar refused to dismount, falsely claiming that the horse belonged to him and accusing the rich man of being a thief.
Q3. How did the Wise Caliph use practical psychology to resolve the dispute?

Ans: The Caliph ordered both men to touch the horse separately in the palace stables. When the beggar approached, the horse neighed angrily and backed away, showing it did not recognize him. When the rich man gently stroked its neck, the horse showed joyful recognition, proving indisputably that the rich man was the true master.
Q4. What verdict did the Caliph deliver, and how did the rich man demonstrate noble character?

Ans: The Caliph restored the horse to the rich traveler and ordered the dishonest beggar to be punished. However, the rich man generously forgave the beggar and gave him a purse of gold coins to assist his livelihood, exemplifying extraordinary Islamic magnanimity.
► 1.2 Speaking: Expressing Polite Agreement and Disagreement on Leadership
► Agreement and Disagreement on Essential Leadership Qualities
Situation: Classroom debate on the most essential quality of a modern political leader:
Usman: In my opinion, sharp economic intellect is the most vital trait for a national leader.
Faisal: I agree that economic knowledge is important; however, I believe unyielding moral integrity and justice, like Caliph Haroon's, are far more crucial.
Usman: You make a compelling argument. Without moral justice, economic wealth can never benefit the common citizen.
► 1.3 Language Practice: Capitalization, Punctuation, and Affixes (Prefixes & Suffixes)

Punctuated: The poet said, "I sought to hear the voice of God, and climbed the topmost steeple."
Unpunctuated: caliph haroon ur rashid ruled the abbasid empire from baghdad with great justice
Punctuated: Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid ruled the Abbasid Empire from Baghdad with great justice.
The Caliph delivered a discerning judgment.
A judge must remain strictly impartial.
The dishonest beggar repented in tears.
The noble traveler was merciful towards the thief.
A faithless companion cannot be trusted.
► 1.4 Writing: A Unified Descriptive Paragraph on 'The Hallmarks of Wise Leadership'
• Descriptive Paragraph: The Hallmarks of Wise Leadership

True leadership is defined not by authoritarian power or lavish privilege, but by moral wisdom, humility, and unwavering dedication to public welfare. A great leader, exemplified historically by Caliph Haroon-ur-Rashid, possesses the discernment to see beyond superficial appearances, listens attentively to the grievances of the poorest citizens, and dispenses justice without fear or favour. Furthermore, as Louis I. Newman's poem reminds us, genuine spiritual leadership requires staying deeply connected with common people rather than remaining detached in ivory towers. By combining sharp intellect with profound empathy, an exemplary leader unites society, safeguards individual human dignity, and leaves behind a legacy of enduring peace.

1. Thematic Cluster: Group related ideas together (e.g. Personal Character, Judicial Decisions, Social Welfare).
2. Hierarchy of Arguments: Place the strongest, most compelling historical evidence at the beginning of body paragraphs.
3. Concluding Synthesis: Ensure the final sentence connects back to the central thesis statement.

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 2LABOUR AND PEOPLE'S RIGHTS(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 2: LABOUR AND PEOPLE'S RIGHTS (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 2.1 Reading Comprehension: Dignity of Work (Islamic Teachings & Modern Values)
■ PRE-READING QUESTIONS & DIGNITY OF LABOUR DISCUSSION
Pre-Reading Q1. What is meant by the phrase 'Dignity of Work' (or Dignity of Labour)?

Ans: Dignity of Work means that all forms of honest labour, whether mental or physical (manual), are noble, honorable, and worthy of profound respect, and that no honest occupation is low or degrading.
Pre-Reading Q2. How did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) and his noble Companions establish the dignity of manual work?

Ans: The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) personally performed household chores, mended his own shoes, milked goats, and joined his companions in digging the Trench during the Battle of Khandaq, teaching that working with one's own hands is beloved to Allah.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN TEXT TABLE
The ethical principle that all honest jobs deserve equal honor and respect
Physical work performed by hands rather than machines or purely mental effort
Work that is falsely perceived as unskilled, low, or degrading by class snobs
A legitimate means of securing financial necessities and food for one's family
A deep, wide defensive ditch dug around Madinah in which the Prophet worked
Relying on one's own capabilities, effort, and hard work rather than charity
High respect, value, and admiration for a person or craft
Work moist flour into dough with hands for baking bread
The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) repaired his own clothes and mended his own shoes.
Caliph Hazrat Abu Bakr (R.A) stopped milking the neighbor's goats after becoming Caliph.
False (F) — He continued milking the neighborhood orphans' goats with humility even after becoming Caliph.
Caliph Hazrat Umar (R.A) carried a heavy sack of flour on his own back to feed starving children.
In developed nations like China and the USA, students proudly perform manual jobs to earn their education.
Islam encourages believers to depend on begging rather than earning an honest livelihood.
False (F) — The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) declared: 'The hand that earns is the friend of Allah.'

MCQ 1. What historic manual task did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) participate in during the Battle of Khandaq?  • a. Sailing ships  • b. Digging the deep defensive trench alongside his companions  • c. Painting walls  • d. Carpentry only
Ans: b. Digging the deep defensive trench alongside his companions

MCQ 2. What famous Hadith summarizes the nobility of earning through honest physical work?  • a. 'Silence is golden'  • b. 'The hand that earns is the beloved friend of Allah'  • c. 'Wealth is power'  • d. 'Travel widely'
Ans: b. 'The hand that earns is the beloved friend of Allah'

MCQ 3. What did Caliph Umar (R.A) do when he found a destitute woman boiling stones to console her hungry children?  • a. Appointed guards  • b. Went directly to the state treasury (Bait-ul-Mal), carried flour and fat on his back, and cooked food himself  • c. Asked neighbors to help  • d. Postponed the matter
Ans: b. Went directly to the state treasury (Bait-ul-Mal), carried flour and fat on his back, and cooked food himself

MCQ 4. How do university students in countries like Japan and the West support their tuition fees?  • a. They depend entirely on loans  • b. They gladly work in restaurants, deliver newspapers, and wash cars without feeling ashamed  • c. They refuse manual work  • d. None of these
Ans: b. They gladly work in restaurants, deliver newspapers, and wash cars without feeling ashamed
Q1. Cite specific historical examples illustrating how the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) dignified everyday manual work.

Ans: The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) never considered any domestic or community chore beneath his dignity. He swept his house, lit the fire, milked his goats, patched his garments, and mended his shoes. During the construction of the Prophet's Mosque (Masjid-e-Nabawi) and the digging of the Trench, he carried heavy bricks and rocks on his shoulders alongside ordinary laborers.
Q2. Describe the incident of Caliph Hazrat Umar (R.A) carrying food supplies for a poor family in the dark.

Ans: While patrolling Madinah at night, Caliph Umar heard children crying in a tent and found their mother boiling water with stones to soothe them to sleep because there was no food. Shaken by his responsibility before Allah, the Caliph rushed to Bait-ul-Mal, loaded a sack of flour and ghee on his own back, delivered it, blew the fire with his own breath, and fed the children until they laughed happily.
Q3. How does the cultural perception of manual work in Western and Far Eastern societies differ from outdated social snobbery?

Ans: In countries like China, Japan, and the USA, dignity of work is universally practiced. University students and professionals take pride in mowing lawns, waiting tables, painting houses, and plumbing without social stigma. Every honest worker is addressed with equal civic respect and paid fair wages.
Q4. What social and economic reforms are needed in our society to establish true dignity of labour?

Ans: We must eliminate feudal snobbery, guarantee fair minimum wages, provide social security and health insurance to sanitary and domestic workers, introduce technical/vocational education in high schools, and treat all laborers with courteous respect.
► 2.2 Speaking: Seeking and Offering Constructive Vocational Advice
Situation: Dialogue between a career counselor and a student seeking advice on vocational technical skills:
Student (Hamid): Sir, my relatives discourage me from pursuing technical electrical engineering, saying it involves manual work.
Counselor: That is an outdated prejudice, Hamid. Highly skilled electrical and solar technicians earn honorable livelihoods and are the backbone of modern industries.
Student (Hamid): Thank you, Sir. Remembering the examples of our great Caliphs gives me immense pride to pursue practical technical mastery.
► 2.3 Language Practice: Common Irregular Verbs, Tenses, and Compound Sentences
■ EXERCISE 1: THREE FORMS OF IRREGULAR VERBS TABLE
The companions dug the protective trench with immense devotion.
The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) swept his own home with humility.
Caliph Umar bore the heavy burden of public welfare.
The believers built the mosque with collective labor.
He fed the hungry children with fresh warm bread.
■ EXERCISE 2: SIMPLE VS COMPOUND SENTENCES TABLE
One independent clause with a subject and predicate
Honest manual labor earns divine blessings.
Two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS)
The work was exhausting, but the workers sang with cheerful spirit.
Islam honors every honest craft, so we must respect all workers.
► 2.4 Writing: Formal Email to the Municipal Commissioner on Sanitary Workers' Safety and Rights
• Formal Email: Municipal Sanitation Workers' Rights
Subject: Urgent Request for Protective Equipment and Medical Insurance for Sanitary Workers
I am writing this email to draw your urgent attention towards the perilous working conditions of our municipal sanitary workers and drain cleaners.

These hardworking individuals perform hazardous civic duties without adequate protective equipment such as oxygen masks, waterproof safety suits, specialized boots, and heavy gloves, exposing them to toxic gases and fatal infections.
In accordance with constitutional labour rights and the timeless Islamic principle of the Dignity of Work, it is the state's ethical duty to safeguard these essential workers.
I request your office to immediately supply certified personal protective equipment (PPE), provide comprehensive health insurance, and ensure fair minimum wages for all municipal workers.
► 2.5 Study Skills: Practical Guidelines for Accurate Official Form Filling
Block Letters: Fill all personal details (Full Name, Father's Name, CNIC, Address) in clear, capitalized BLOCK LETTERS.
No Overwriting: Avoid crossing out or using correction fluid on official examination or vocational registration forms.
Mandatory Fields: Ensure all asterisks (*) and date fields (DD/MM/YYYY) are correctly filled before signing.
► 2.6 Fun: Dignity of Labour Proverbs & Maxims
• 'No honest craft is mean; the only real disgrace is idleness.'
• 'The hand that works is holier than the lips that pray without action.'
• 'Sweat of honest labour smells sweeter than stolen perfume.'

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 3PRACTICING POSITIVE WORK ETHICS(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 3: PRACTICING POSITIVE WORK ETHICS (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 3.1 Reading Comprehension: King Bruce and the Spider (Poem by Eliza Cook)
Pre-Reading Q1. What does the historical legend of King Robert Bruce and the spider teach us about resilience?
Ans: The legend teaches that temporary defeat is not the end of a noble pursuit; through patience, persistence, and continuous effort, even insurmountable obstacles can eventually be overcome.
Pre-Reading Q2. Who was King Robert Bruce, and what situation was he facing when he observed the spider?

Ans: Robert Bruce was the King of Scotland who was fighting to liberate his nation from foreign rule. After suffering six consecutive military defeats, he was hiding in a desolate mountain cave, on the verge of despair.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN POEM TABLE
A sovereign head of state, especially a king or queen
The complete loss or absence of hope
Throw or cast with great force or determination
A very fine, strong cord made by a spider to spin its web
A reward, recompense, or prize for hard work
Persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success
Overcome and take control of a problem or enemy by military or moral force
Climb or move with difficulty, using hands and feet
King Robert Bruce was hiding in a royal palace when he felt discouraged.
False (F) — He was hiding in a lonely, gloomy cave in the mountains.
The spider attempted to reach its web repeatedly despite falling down nine times.
The spider gave up its goal after failing on the eighth attempt.
False (F) — It persevered until it successfully swung to the beam on the tenth attempt.
King Bruce was inspired by the tiny creature's steadfast determination.
King Bruce rallied his men after this incident and successfully freed Scotland.
MCQ 1. Who is the poet of the famous poem 'King Bruce and the Spider'?  • a. Eliza Cook  • b. Louis I. Newman  • c. William Shakespeare  • d. Robert Frost

MCQ 2. What made King Bruce feel so despondent inside the cave?  • a. He had lost his crown and failed six times in battle to free his people  • b. He was hungry  • c. He had lost his way in the forest  • d. His horse was injured
Ans: a. He had lost his crown and failed six times in battle to free his people

MCQ 3. What was the spider trying to accomplish on the roof beam?  • a. Catch an insect  • b. Fasten its thread to the roof to complete its web  • c. Escape from a predator  • d. Build a nest for winter
Ans: b. Fasten its thread to the roof to complete its web

MCQ 4. What universal proverb did King Bruce formulate after watching the spider succeed?  • a. 'Time and tide wait for none'  • b. 'All that glitters is not gold'  • c. 'If at first you don't succeed, try, try again'  • d. 'Honesty is the best policy'
Ans: c. 'If at first you don't succeed, try, try again'
Q1. Describe the emotional state of King Robert Bruce before he noticed the spider in the cave.

Ans: King Bruce was in a state of profound despair and grief. Having fought six brave battles to liberate his Scottish countrymen from foreign domination and having been defeated each time, he believed his cause was hopelessly lost and contemplated surrendering his lifelong mission.
Q2. Explain how the tiny spider demonstrated the virtue of positive work ethics and persistence.

Ans: The spider was attempting to anchor its fine silken thread to a high roof beam. It slipped, tumbled, and fell down nine consecutive times. Instead of giving up or showing frustration, the tiny creature patiently began its climb anew each time until, on the tenth attempt, it successfully reached the beam and secured its web.
Q3. What profound life lesson did King Bruce derive from the spider's triumph?

Ans: King Bruce realized that if a tiny, fragile insect could show such unyielding perseverance without complaining of failure, a human monarch leading an entire nation should never surrender to temporary adversity. He learned that persistent effort transforms apparent impossibility into glorious victory.
Q4. How did this encounter alter the course of Scottish history?

Ans: Revitalized by renewed faith and courage, King Bruce emerged from the cave, called upon his dispersed Scottish warriors, organized a spirited resistance, and led his army to a decisive triumph at the Battle of Bannockburn, securing Scotland's sovereignty.
► 3.2 Speaking: Expressing Academic and Personal Needs with Valid Justifications
Situation: Dialogue between a student and a teacher requesting permission to utilize the school science lab after class hours:
Bilal: Good afternoon, Sir. I need special permission to work in the physics laboratory for an extra hour after school today.
Teacher: Good afternoon, Bilal. What is the specific reason for this extended laboratory time?
Bilal: Sir, our science exhibition project on renewable solar models requires precise electrical circuit testing, which cannot be done safely at home.
Teacher: That is a very valid and commendable justification. I will inform the lab assistant to assist and supervise you until 3:30 PM.
► 3.3 Language Practice: Past Tenses & Master Rules of Definite/Indefinite Articles
King Bruce watched the persistent spider in the cave.
The soldiers were retreating when night fell.
The spider had fallen nine times before it finally succeeded.
King Bruce had been agonizing over his defeats for hours.
■ EXERCISE 2: MASTER RULES OF ARTICLES TABLE
Robert Bruce was _____ King of Scotland.
Definite article used before unique royal title of a specific nation
He observed _____ tiny spider swinging across the beam.
Indefinite article used before a singular countable noun with a consonant sound
It was _____ inspiring example of unyielding determination.
Indefinite article used before a vowel sound ('in-')
_____ perseverance always leads to ultimate triumph.
No article before abstract uncountable nouns used in a general sense
_____ Scottish soldiers fought bravely in the decisive battle.
Definite article referring to a specific group of national soldiers
► 3.4 Writing: Comprehensive Summary of Eliza Cook's 'King Bruce and the Spider'
• Summary: King Bruce and the Spider (by Eliza Cook)

Eliza Cook's inspirational ballad 'King Bruce and the Spider' narrates a poignant historical incident from the life of Robert Bruce, King of Scotland. After being vanquished six times on the battlefield, the despairing monarch sought refuge inside a gloomy mountain cave, ready to abandon all hope of freeing his homeland. While lying in deep contemplation, he noticed a tiny spider trying to reach a beam above to weave its web. The insect slipped and fell nine times in succession, yet it never yielded to frustration. With tireless resilience, the spider climbed once more and triumphed on its tenth attempt. Deeply moved by this extraordinary display of perseverance, King Bruce banished his gloom, resolved to try again, rallied his countrymen, and achieved total victory for Scotland. The poem immortalizes the enduring moral maxim: 'If at first you don't succeed, try, try again.'
► 3.5 Study Skills: Unleashing Creative Expression through Free Writing
1. Continuous Flow: Write non-stop for 5 to 10 minutes without pausing to self-censor, correct grammar, or erase words.
2. Thought Stream: Allow ideas, metaphors, and sensory details to emerge naturally on the paper.
3. Post-Writing Review: Read through the raw text, highlight the most vivid phrases, and organize them into coherent paragraphs.
► 3.6 Fun: High-Impact Collocations on Work Ethics
Unyielding Determination: Holding firmly to a noble goal regardless of hardships
Strenuous Effort: Putting in vigorous, dedicated physical or mental work
Decisive Victory: An unmistakable, complete triumph over difficulty
Inspiring Resilience: The admirable capacity to recover quickly from setbacks
Golden Opportunity: An exceptionally favorable chance for progress and success

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 4MEDIA FOR INFORMATION AND REFLECTION(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 4: MEDIA FOR INFORMATION AND REFLECTION (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 4.1 Reading Comprehension: Social Media: Opportunities, Challenges, and Digital Responsibility
Pre-Reading Q1. How has social media transformed modern global communication and learning?

Ans: Social media has eliminated geographical barriers, enabling instantaneous information exchange, collaborative global education, civic awareness, and creative entrepreneurship across billions of people.
Pre-Reading Q2. What potential hazards and ethical dilemmas accompany unrestrained social media usage?
Ans: Unregulated use can lead to digital addiction, cyberbullying, spread of disinformation/fake news, privacy breaches, mental distress, and erosion of genuine face-to-face social bonds.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN DIGITAL MEDIA TABLE
The use of electronic communication to intimidate, harass, or demean someone
The permanent record of a user's digital activities, actions, and uploads online
False information deliberately created and spread to deceive or mislead people
Automated computing rules used by platforms to curate personalized feeds and content
The customary code of polite and ethical behavior among internet users
An online environment where a person encounters only opinions that reflect their own
A social network of individuals who interact online around shared interests
The ability to critically identify, evaluate, and utilize credible digital information
Social media platforms only provide entertainment and have no educational value.
False (F) — They offer immense educational resources, scholarly webinars, and learning groups.
Everything shared or posted online contributes to a permanent digital footprint.
Cyberbullying cannot cause serious psychological harm because it happens online.
False (F) — Cyberbullying can inflict severe emotional trauma, anxiety, and depression on victims.
Fact-checking news before sharing it is a hallmark of responsible digital citizenship.
Spending excessive time on social media can disrupt sleep patterns and academic focus.

MCQ 1. What constitutes a user's 'Digital Footprint'?  • a. The physical size of a computer monitor  • b. The cumulative trail of data, comments, and photos left by online activity  • c. The brand of internet router  • d. A digital password
Ans: b. The cumulative trail of data, comments, and photos left by online activity

MCQ 2. What is the primary danger of spreading unverified news on social networks?  • a. High internet bills  • b. Rapid propagation of panic, social friction, and false rumors  • c. Computer memory loss  • d. Slower typing speed
Ans: b. Rapid propagation of panic, social friction, and false rumors

MCQ 3. Which of the following demonstrates excellent 'Netiquette'?  • a. Posting abusive comments anonymously  • b. Using respectful language, verifying facts, and protecting personal privacy  • c. Forwarding chain messages blindly  • d. Sharing friends' private photos without consent
Ans: b. Using respectful language, verifying facts, and protecting personal privacy

MCQ 4. How can students leverage social media positively for academic advancement?  • a. By joining educational webinars, academic research groups, and skill workshops  • b. By playing online games all night  • c. By scrolling endlessly without purpose  • d. By arguing with strangers online
Ans: a. By joining educational webinars, academic research groups, and skill workshops
Q1. Analyze the major educational and professional benefits of modern social media networks.

Ans: Social media serves as a dynamic catalyst for knowledge sharing, remote learning, and professional networking. Students gain access to international educational lectures, digital libraries, and global collaborative projects, while professionals and young entrepreneurs utilize these platforms for global marketing, freelancing, and career development.
Q2. Explain the negative psychological and social consequences of compulsive social media use.

Ans: Compulsive usage often results in reduced attention spans, severe sleep deprivation, social isolation, and heightened anxiety. Constant exposure to idealized portrayals of others' lives fosters unrealistic social comparisons and low self-esteem among impressionable teenagers.
Q3. What proactive measures should individuals take to protect themselves against cyber threats and scams?

Ans: Users should configure strong, distinct passwords with two-factor authentication, adjust privacy settings to restrict public viewing of personal details, avoid clicking suspicious links or downloading unverified attachments, and immediately block and report abusive accounts.
Q4. Discuss the concept of 'Digital Citizenship' and its core responsibilities.

Ans: Digital citizenship embodies the ethical, safe, and legal engagement with internet technologies. Responsible digital citizens respect intellectual property, practice courteous netiquette, verify news authenticity before sharing, promote positive discourse, and actively combat online bullying.
► 4.2 Speaking: Delivering a Structured Oral Presentation on 'Combating Cyberbullying'
► Assembly Speech: Combating Cyberbullying and Safe Digital Culture
Situation: Script for an individual 3-minute presentation delivered during School Morning Assembly:
Speaker (Student): Respected Teachers and Dear Fellow Students: Today, I stand before you to speak on 'Combating Cyberbullying and Building a Safe Digital Culture.'

Speaker (Student): While digital technology connects us, unkind words posted behind the shield of computer screens inflict real, profound emotional pain. Cruelty online is not harmless banter; it leaves invisible scars on young hearts.

Speaker (Student): Let us make a united commitment: before we hit 'send' or 'comment', let us ask ourselves: Is it true? Is it necessary? Is it kind? Let us use our digital voices to uplift, encourage, and inspire our peers.
► 4.3 Language Practice: Future Tenses & Active / Passive Voice Mastery
Responsible citizens will verify news before posting.
Students will be attending an online seminar tomorrow.
By 2030, digital classrooms will have transformed education.
By next month, she will have been managing the blog for a year.
■ EXERCISE 2: ACTIVE TO PASSIVE VOICE TRANSFORMATION TABLE
Millions of people use social media daily.
Social media is used daily by millions of people.
The committee launched a cyber safety campaign.
A cyber safety campaign was launched by the committee.
The IT experts are developing new security filters.
New security filters are being developed by the IT experts.
The school will host an informative workshop on AI.
An informative workshop on AI will be hosted by the school.
Cybercriminals have hacked several sensitive accounts.
Several sensitive accounts have been hacked by cybercriminals.
► 4.4 Writing: A Comprehensive Cause-and-Effect Essay on 'The Impact of Social Media on Youth'
• Cause and Effect Essay: Impact of Social Media on Youth

The meteoric rise of social media platforms has revolutionized how modern adolescents communicate, learn, and perceive the world around them. One primary cause for its widespread adoption is the human desire for instant connectivity and community belonging. Consequently, young people can collaborate globally, share creative projects, and access vast educational resources instantaneously. However, this unprecedented connectivity also carries severe negative repercussions. Compulsive social media consumption frequently causes academic distraction, sleep deprivation, and reduced physical activity. Furthermore, exposure to unverified misinformation and cyberbullying often leads to psychological distress, anxiety, and distorted self-image among teenagers. To maximize the benefits while neutralizing these hazards, schools and parents must foster critical media literacy, promote time-management boundaries, and guide youth toward balanced, purposeful digital engagement.
► 4.5 Study Skills: The 5-Step Critical Thinking Framework for Digital Information
1. Source Verification: Examine the author's credentials, publisher reputation, and date of publication.
2. Evidence Cross-Checking: Corroborate claims with at least two independent, peer-reviewed, or established journalistic sources.
3. Bias Detection: Identify whether the content uses emotional manipulation, loaded vocabulary, or selective statistics.
4. Alternative Perspectives: Evaluate contrary arguments and assess underlying logical assumptions.
5. Reasoned Conclusion: Formulate an objective judgment grounded strictly in verified evidence.
► 4.6 Fun: Future Vision Profile — 'A Decade Ahead'
Career Aspiration: Leading Software Architect & Educational Content Creator
Societal Contribution: Establishing free coding academies and digital literacy hubs in rural Sindh
Personal Philosophy: Using technology as a noble instrument to eradicate ignorance and empower underprivileged communities

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 5RESPECTING SELF AND OTHERS(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 5: RESPECTING SELF AND OTHERS (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 5.1 Reading Comprehension: A Bad Dream: Cultivating Empathy and Ending School Bullying
Pre-Reading Q1. Why is mutual respect and empathy essential for a healthy school learning environment?
Ans: Mutual respect creates a safe, nurturing environment where every student feels valued, confident, and free from fear or intimidation, fostering academic excellence and emotional well-being.
Pre-Reading Q2. What is the psychological root behind bullying behavior, and how does a bad dream spark self-realization?

Ans: Bullying often stems from a desire for dominance or unaddressed personal insecurities; experiencing a vivid nightmare where the bully becomes the helpless victim sparks deep remorse and moral awakening.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN STORY TABLE
Frighten or threaten someone, usually to force them to do what one wants
A terrifying dream that produces intense feelings of fear or helplessness
Deep and painful regret for having committed a wrong or hurtful action
Sympathetic pity and concern for the sufferings or misfortunes of others
A person who is harmed, injured, or bullied by another
The restoration of friendly relations and harmony after a conflict
A person or group that initiates an unprovoked attack or hostile act
Confidence in one's own worth, abilities, and self-respect
The protagonist in 'A Bad Dream' frequently mocked and teased his weaker classmates.
In his dream, the protagonist was praised and rewarded for his arrogance.
False (F) — In his dream, he experienced the terrifying sensation of being friendless and bullied.
The terrifying dream led to a profound transformation in his attitude toward others.
Bullying has no long-term psychological impact on school children.
False (F) — Bullying can cause enduring trauma, academic decline, and severe anxiety.
The protagonist apologized sincerely to his classmates upon waking up.

MCQ 1. What dramatic experience made the arrogant boy realize the cruelty of his actions?  • a. A strict warning from the principal  • b. A terrifying nightmare where he felt the acute agony of being bullied  • c. Losing a football match  • d. Failing an exam
Ans: b. A terrifying nightmare where he felt the acute agony of being bullied

MCQ 2. What is the central theme of 'A Bad Dream'?  • a. The importance of early morning exercise  • b. Cultivating empathy, respecting others, and rejecting toxic bullying  • c. Ancient legends  • d. Space exploration
Ans: b. Cultivating empathy, respecting others, and rejecting toxic bullying

MCQ 3. How did the boy act the morning after having the nightmare?  • a. He refused to go to school  • b. He went to school with humility, sought forgiveness from his peers, and became a supportive friend  • c. He blamed his brother  • d. He stayed angry
Ans: b. He went to school with humility, sought forgiveness from his peers, and became a supportive friend

MCQ 4. What should a student do when witnessing a classmate being bullied?  • a. Join the bullies  • b. Stand by silently and film the event  • c. Speak up safely, support the victim, and immediately notify school authorities  • d. Laugh aloud
Ans: c. Speak up safely, support the victim, and immediately notify school authorities
Q1. Detail the habitual behavior of the protagonist towards his peers before the nightmare.

Ans: Before his transformative dream, the protagonist behaved with cruel arrogance. He frequently mocked classmates for their physical appearance, made sarcastic remarks about their academic abilities, and derived perverse satisfaction from intimidating younger students.
Q2. Describe the vivid events of the nightmare and the emotions it evoked in the protagonist.

Ans: In the nightmare, roles were completely inverted. The protagonist found himself stranded in an unfamiliar, hostile schoolyard where everyone pointed fingers, laughed at his distress, and refused him shelter. He felt overwhelming dread, isolation, and helpless terror, realizing for the first time the excruciating agony his victims endured.
Q3. How does empathy serve as the ultimate antidote to interpersonal cruelty?

Ans: Empathy enables an individual to psychologically place themselves in another person's position and feel their pain. Once a person truly understands the emotional suffering caused by cruel behavior, their conscience makes it impossible to continue inflicting that pain on others.
Q4. What steps can schools implement to establish a zero-tolerance culture against bullying?

Ans: Schools should institute clear anti-bullying codes of conduct, conduct regular moral awareness assemblies, establish confidential grievance reporting channels, train peer counselors, and promote inclusive teamwork through collaborative projects and sports.
► 5.2 Speaking: Providing Constructive Peer Feedback on Classroom Presentations
Situation: Peer evaluation dialogue following an anti-bullying presentation in English class:
Ayesha: Zainab, your presentation on emotional resilience was exceptionally well-structured and confident.
Zainab: Thank you, Ayesha! What specific area do you think I can improve upon for the inter-school contest?
Ayesha: Your vocal modulation and slide clarity were great; however, maintaining more steady eye contact with the audience on the left side of the room will make your delivery even more impactful.
Zainab: That is an excellent observation. I will certainly incorporate your feedback during our rehearsals.
► 5.3 Language Practice: Number of Nouns (Pluralization Rules) & Modal Verbs Mastery
■ EXERCISE 1: REGULAR & IRREGULAR NOUN PLURALS TABLE
All children deserve a safe classroom environment.
The selection criteria must be strictly merit-based.
Bullying is a distressing social phenomenon.
Their psychological analyses revealed the trauma.
■ EXERCISE 2: MODAL VERBS IN CONTEXT TABLE
Students must treat all peers with unconditional dignity.
We should apologize promptly whenever we hurt someone.
Empathy can heal broken relationships and build trust.
Could you please help me understand this concept?
Kind words may brighten a depressed person's entire day.
► 5.4 Writing: Formal Letter to the Editor on 'Tackling Bullying in Educational Institutions'
• Formal Letter to Editor: Tackling Bullying in Schools
Subject: Urgent Need to Eradicate Bullying in Educational Institutions
Through the esteemed columns of your widely circulated newspaper, I wish to draw the urgent attention of educational authorities and parents toward the growing menace of bullying in schools.

Bullying—whether verbal, physical, or cyber—inflicts severe psychological trauma on impressionable young students. It leads to chronic anxiety, academic deterioration, school absenteeism, and long-term depression. Many victims suffer in silence due to fear of reprisal and the absence of institutional support mechanisms.

To safeguard our children's future, every school must enforce a strict, zero-tolerance anti-bullying policy. Educational boards should mandate professional student counseling centers, provide anonymous reporting channels, and organize regular character-building workshops. Parents and teachers must work closely to nurture emotional intelligence and empathy among youth.
I sincerely hope the authorities will take proactive measures to make our educational campuses safe havens of learning and mutual respect.
Student, Government Comprehensive High School, Karachi.
