content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 6CHARACTER BUILDING(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
► 6.1 Reading Comprehension: Speak Gently (Poem by David Bates / G. W. Langford)
Pre-Reading Q1. Why is the power of gentle and courteous speech regarded as the cornerstone of moral character?
Ans: Gentle speech disarms hostility, soothes aching hearts, preserves human dignity, and builds unbreakable bonds of mutual love and trust without costing any material wealth.
Pre-Reading Q2. What impact do harsh, impulsive words have on human relationships and inner peace?
Ans: Harsh words inflict deep emotional wounds, breed lingering resentment, ruin familial and social harmony, and leave behind profound regret that cannot easily be undone.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN POEM TABLE
To converse with soft, courteous, and compassionate tones
To impair, spoil, damage, or disfigure the beauty or goodness of something
To feel or cause to feel deep sorrow, distress, or sadness
Infinite or unending time; the eternal afterlife in divine presence
Great energy, passion, and enthusiasm in pursuit of a cause or objective
A distinctive way of pronouncing a language or expressing emotion
To remain in existence; to undergo hardship patiently without giving up
Gentle, temperate, and calm in nature, tone, or disposition
According to the poet, gentle speech is much more effective than harsh force.
The poet advises us to speak harshly to little children so they obey rules quickly.
False (F) — The poet urges: 'Speak gently to the little child; its love be sure to gain.'
Old people who have endured life's burdens deserve our utmost tenderness.
Harsh words once spoken can be easily erased without causing any lasting pain.
False (F) — Harsh words inflict permanent emotional scars and drive hearts away.
A gentle word is an enduring investment whose reward extends into eternity.
MCQ 1. Who is the author of the timeless moral poem 'Speak Gently'?  • a. David Bates  • b. Louis I. Newman  • c. Eliza Cook  • d. William Blake

MCQ 2. Why should we speak gently to the young and little children?  • a. Because their hearts are tender and early impressions last throughout their lives  • b. Because they do not understand English  • c. To make them sleep  • d. None of these
Ans: a. Because their hearts are tender and early impressions last throughout their lives

MCQ 3. How should we address the elderly and infirm members of our society?  • a. With impatient loudness  • b. With gentle, loving reverence as they near the end of life's journey  • c. By ignoring them  • d. With strict commands
Ans: b. With gentle, loving reverence as they near the end of life's journey

MCQ 4. What eternal reward does the poem promise for cultivating gentle speech?  • a. Wealth and political crowns  • b. Peace of conscience, lasting affection of fellow beings, and divine pleasure in eternity  • c. Physical strength  • d. Fame in newspapers
Ans: b. Peace of conscience, lasting affection of fellow beings, and divine pleasure in eternity
Q1. What central philosophy does the poet express regarding the rule of love versus the rule of fear?

Ans: The poet asserts that true moral authority is established through love, kindness, and gentle persuasion rather than through harsh coercion or fear. Harsh words destroy goodwill and incite rebellion, whereas gentle speech wins lasting devotion and loyalty.
Q2. Explain the specific advice the poet offers regarding interactions with the aged, the poor, and the erring.

Ans: The poet advises us to treat the elderly with profound reverence because their earthly journey is nearly over; to speak mildly to the poor so they do not feel humiliated by their misfortune; and to address those who have made moral errors with tender compassion to gently guide them back to righteousness.
Q3. How does speech reflect a person's inner character and moral refinement?

Ans: A person's language and tone are direct reflections of their heart. Courteous, humble, and considerate speech demonstrates self-discipline, emotional maturity, and deep empathy, while vulgar, arrogant, and abrasive words reveal an unrefined, insecure ego.
Q4. Summarize the ultimate message conveyed in the closing stanza regarding eternity.

Ans: The closing stanza reveals that a simple act of gentle speech is a spiritual treasure. Though softly uttered in a transient earthly moment, the love, comfort, and goodwill it fosters echo perpetually, yielding eternal blessings in the life hereafter.
► 6.2 Speaking: Delivering an Inspiring Speech on 'The Power of Polite Words'
► Declamation Speech: The Power of Polite Words
Situation: Extract from a declamation speech presented in the Inter-School Championship:

Orator (Student): Mr. President, Respected Teachers, and Honored Guests: Words have the immense power to build bridges or ignite wars. A single harsh syllable can shatter a lifelong bond, while a word spoken in gentle sincerity can heal a broken soul.

Orator (Student): Let us remember that true strength is never noisy or cruel. The greatest leaders throughout history—from the Holy Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) to great statesmen—conquered hearts through impeccable courtesy, patience, and gentle wisdom.
Orator (Student): Let our speech be a soothing balm for those in despair, an encouraging guide for the young, and a source of light wherever we go. Thank you.
► 6.3 Language Practice: Transitional Devices & Direct / Indirect Questions Mastery
■ EXERCISE 1: TRANSITIONAL DEVICES OF ORDER & REASON TABLE
First and foremost, we must treat elders with unreserved respect.
Furthermore, gentle speech prevents unnecessary domestic disputes.
He spoke kindly; consequently, all hostility vanished.
Owing to her soothing manner, the frightened child stopped crying.
In conclusion, character is forged through persistent moral discipline.
■ EXERCISE 2: DIRECT TO INDIRECT QUESTIONS TABLE
Could you please tell me where the library is located?
Inversion removed; normal word order (Subject + Verb)
Why was the monarch in despair?
I wonder why the monarch was in despair.
Did the spider complete its web?
Do you know if the spider completed its web?
How can we build moral character?
Could you explain how we can build moral character?
What time does the assembly begin?
May I ask what time the assembly begins?
► 6.4 Writing: A Structured Expository Essay on 'The Role of Character Building in National Development'
• Expository Essay: Role of Character Building in National Development

The strength and greatness of a nation are measured not by its material wealth or monumental skyscrapers, but by the moral character, integrity, and discipline of its citizens. Character building is the systematic cultivation of core ethical virtues—honesty, empathy, civility, justice, and diligent work ethics—within individuals from early childhood. When youth are educated with sound moral values alongside scientific knowledge, they grow into responsible citizens who reject corruption, respect the rule of law, and prioritize collective national progress over selfish gain. Conversely, a society that neglects character education experiences social decay, civic apathy, and institutional collapse despite technological advancement. Therefore, educational institutions, families, and media must collaboratively integrate character-building curricula that foster compassion, civic accountability, and dedicated patriotism.
► 6.5 Study Skills: Conducting a Personal SWOC (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Challenges) Analysis
Diligent study habits, polite communication, and empathy
Leverage these strengths to mentor peers and lead student clubs.
Tendency to procrastinate on complex math tasks
Implement the Pomodoro technique and maintain a strict daily log.
Availability of digital educational webinars and science fairs
Participate actively in provincial competitions to enhance skills.
Establish fixed offline study zones and disable non-academic alerts.
► 6.6 Fun: 'The Path of Honor' — Moral Decision Scenarios
Scenario A: You find an expensive lost watch in the school library.: Honorable Choice: Immediately submit it to the Principal's office with date and location noted.
Scenario B: A classmate spreads an unkind rumor about your friend.: Honorable Choice: Defend your friend politely, stop the rumor from spreading, and advise the speaker gently.
Scenario C: Your team is losing a debate competition due to a timer error.: Honorable Choice: Accept the judges' final verdict gracefully without displaying bitterness or anger.

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 7PRAISING NATURE(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
► 7.1 Reading Comprehension: My Travel Diary: Journey to the Gorakh Hills Station (The Murree of Sindh)
Pre-Reading Q1. What unique geographical characteristics make the Gorakh Hill Station a magnificent jewel of Sindh?

Ans: Situated in the Kirthar Mountain Range at an altitude of over 5,688 feet in Dadu District, Gorakh Hill Station offers cool, sub-zero winter temperatures, breathtaking panoramic valleys, and scenic star-filled skies, earning it the title 'The Murree of Sindh.'
Pre-Reading Q2. How does spending time in serene natural landscapes benefit human mental and physical health?

Ans: Immersion in pristine nature reduces stress, cleanses the lungs with fresh mountain air, revitalizes mental creativity, and evokes profound spiritual appreciation for the Creator's marvelous design.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN TRAVEL DIARY TABLE
An extensive, relatively flat elevated landform with steep sides
The vertical height of an object or point in relation to sea level
An extremely sharp, U-shaped curve in a steep mountain roadway
Providing an unbroken, wide-angle view of an entire surrounding region
Responsible travel to natural areas that conserves the environment
Observing celestial stars, planets, and constellations in the night sky
Following a twisting, curving, or undulating path
The friendly and generous reception and entertainment of guests and travelers
Gorakh Hill Station is situated in the mighty Himalayan Mountain Range.
False (F) — It is situated in the rugged Kirthar Mountain Range of Sindh.
Gorakh Hill has an elevation of approximately 5,688 feet above sea level.
Ordinary small family cars can easily climb the final rugged mountain ascent to Gorakh.
False (F) — Heavy-duty 4x4 off-road vehicles (Jeeps) are required to navigate the steep terrain from Wahi Pandi.
Temperatures at Gorakh Hill can drop below freezing point during winter months.
The author's travel diary details sunrise views, local folk culture, and night camping.
MCQ 1. In which administrative district of Sindh is the Gorakh Hill Station located?  • a. Dadu District  • b. Thatta District  • c. Sukkur District  • d. Hyderabad District

MCQ 2. What is the popular moniker given to the Gorakh Hill Station due to its pleasant, cool climate?  • a. The Oasis of Thar  • b. The Murree of Sindh  • c. The Pearl of Arabian Sea  • d. The Roof of the World
Ans: b. The Murree of Sindh
MCQ 3. Which small town serves as the primary base camp where travelers switch to rugged 4x4 jeeps?  • a. Sehwan  • b. Wahi Pandi  • c. Johi  • d. Bhan Saeedabad

MCQ 4. What breathtaking natural spectacle did the travelers witness at dawn from the summit?  • a. A dust storm  • b. A magnificent golden sunrise illuminating the rolling sea of clouds below  • c. A volcanic eruption  • d. Heavy snowfall
Ans: b. A magnificent golden sunrise illuminating the rolling sea of clouds below
Q1. Describe the thrilling travel route and terrain from Karachi/Hyderabad to the summit of Gorakh Hill.

Ans: The journey proceeds along the Indus Highway toward Dadu and Johi, reaching the base camp at Wahi Pandi. From there, travelers board specialized 4x4 jeeps to tackle the exhilarating, steep 45-kilometer mountain track featuring rugged terrain, hairpin turns, and breathtaking limestone cliffs leading to the plateau summit.
Q2. Explain why Gorakh Hill is regarded as a premier ecotourism and stargazing destination.

Ans: With minimal light pollution, pristine unpolluted atmosphere, and wide horizons at 5,688 feet, Gorakh Hill provides an unparalleled celestial vista of the Milky Way, meteor showers, and constellations. Its untouched natural ecology also offers serene camping and hiking opportunities for nature enthusiasts.
Q3. What infrastructural enhancements can elevate Gorakh Hill into an international tourist resort?

Ans: The government can construct smoother, safety-barricaded roads, establish sustainable eco-resorts with solar power and water desalination, set up emergency medical clinics, provide waste management facilities, and promote local handicrafts and guided cultural tours.
Q4. How does keeping a personal travel diary enhance a student's observation and writing skills?

Ans: A travel diary encourages meticulous attention to sensory details (colors, aromas, temperatures, sounds), fosters chronological organization of experiences, enriches descriptive vocabulary, and preserves precious cultural memories for lifelong reflection.
► 7.2 Speaking: Using Polite Forms to Negotiate and Reach Consensus on a Study Tour
Situation: Student committee meeting discussing the destination for the annual school excursion:
Hamza: I suggest we arrange our three-day annual excursion to the historic sites of Mohenjo-Daro.
Sara: Mohenjo-Daro is wonderful historically; however, since our theme is praising nature, wouldn't Gorakh Hill Station offer a richer experience of mountain ecology and climate?
Hamza: That is a very persuasive point. Could we perhaps visit Sehwan Sharif en route to Gorakh Hill to balance historical heritage and natural beauty?
Sara: That sounds like a perfect consensus! Let us finalize the itinerary and submit it to our principal.
► 7.3 Language Practice: Prepositions of Direction, Compound Prepositions & Type 3 Conditionals
The cool mountain breeze blew softly across the ridge.
We pitched our camping tents in front of the viewpoint.
The guide traveled along with our tourist group.
The road was thrilling because of the steep curves.
The jeep climbed steadily towards the summit.
If we had hired an ordinary car,
we would have failed to climb the mountain track.
We hired a 4x4 jeep, so we climbed successfully.
If they had departed at dawn,
they would have reached the summit before sunset.
They departed late, so they arrived after dark.
the road to Gorakh would have become slippery.
It did not rain, so the drive remained safe.
If you had brought your warm jacket,
you would not have felt the chilly night wind.
You forgot the jacket, so you felt cold.
If we had carried a telescope,
we would have observed the lunar craters clearly.
We lacked a telescope, so we viewed stars with naked eyes.
► 7.4 Writing: A Persuasive Essay on 'Promoting Sustainable Ecotourism at Gorakh Hill Station'
• Persuasive Essay: Promoting Ecotourism at Gorakh Hill Station

Nestled majestically amidst the Kirthar Mountain Range at an elevation of 5,688 feet, Gorakh Hill Station represents one of Sindh's most extraordinary natural treasures. Often hailed as 'The Murree of Sindh', this stunning high-altitude plateau offers visitors cool mountain breezes, breathtaking golden sunrises, and world-class stargazing vistas that rival any international hill resort. Developing sustainable ecotourism at Gorakh Hill would yield tremendous socio-economic benefits. It would generate thousands of hospitality jobs for local communities in Dadu District, revitalize regional transport, and generate substantial revenue for the provincial tourism sector. However, tourism development must strictly respect environmental preservation. Authorities must install solar-powered accommodations, establish strict anti-littering regulations, and protect the fragile indigenous flora and fauna. By investing in eco-friendly infrastructure and promoting responsible travel, we can transform Gorakh Hill into an eco-paradise that showcases Pakistan's breathtaking natural heritage to the world.
► 7.5 Study Skills: Key Elements of an Authentic Personal Travel Diary
1. Date, Time & Location Header: Always begin entries with precise temporal and geographical coordinates (e.g. 'Friday, 15th October, 10:00 PM — Gorakh Top Camp').
2. Rich Sensory Imagery: Incorporate vivid descriptions of what you saw (golden clouds), heard (howling wind), and felt (crisp sub-zero chill).
3. Honest Emotional Reflections: Record personal epiphanies, challenges overcome during travel, and spiritual gratitude for nature's majesty.
Summit: Peak, Apex, Crest, Mountain Top, Zenith
Breeze: Gust, Zephyr, Draft, Chill, Fresh Air
Celestial: Stars, Constellations, Milky Way, Nebula, Cosmos
Valley: Gorge, Canyon, Ravine, Basin, Meadow
Plateau: Tableland, Highland, Mesa, Elevated Plain

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS X ENGLISH — UNIT 8CIVIC SENSE AND CIVIC ACTIVITIES(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 8: CIVIC SENSE AND CIVIC ACTIVITIES (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 8.1 Reading Comprehension: Safety Measures That Can Save Your Life (Disaster Management, Fire & Traffic Safety)
Pre-Reading Q1. What constitutes 'Civic Sense' and why is adherence to public safety protocols vital for a civilized society?

Ans: Civic sense is the social responsibility, law-abiding mindset, and consideration shown by individuals toward fellow citizens; adherence to safety protocols minimizes preventable accidents, saves lives during crises, and maintains orderly public life.
Pre-Reading Q2. How do standard emergency safety drills (such as earthquake and fire drills) protect students in schools?
Ans: Regular drills train students to react calmly, avoid stampedes, use designated fire exits, and execute life-saving maneuvers (like Drop, Cover, and Hold On) during sudden real-world disasters.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN SAFETY TEXT TABLE
The immediate, organized removal of persons from an area of danger
A portable device that discharges foam, gas, or powder to put out fires
The standard safety protocol executed during earthquake tremors
Immediate, basic medical assistance given to an injured person before professional help arrives
A potential source of danger, harm, or adverse health effect on someone
A person walking along a road or in a developed area rather than traveling in a vehicle
Capable of catching fire and burning easily
The act of reviving someone from unconsciousness or apparent death (e.g. CPR)
Using elevators during an active building fire is the safest way to escape.
False (F) — Never use elevators during a fire; always use marked emergency staircases.
During an earthquake tremor, you should 'Drop, Cover, and Hold On' under sturdy furniture.
Water should never be thrown on an electrical or oil/grease fire.
True (T) — Water conducts electricity and spreads oil fires; use Class C/B dry chemical extinguishers instead.
Pedestrians should cross busy roadways anywhere without using zebra crossings.
False (F) — Pedestrians must use designated zebra crossings and overhead pedestrian bridges.
Keeping emergency contact numbers (Rescue 1122, Fire Brigade 16, Police 15) memorized saves critical time.

MCQ 1. What is the primary universal action to perform when an earthquake strikes indoors?  • a. Run toward windows  • b. Drop to the ground, Cover under a sturdy table, and Hold On  • c. Stand in the center of the room  • d. Use the elevator
Ans: b. Drop to the ground, Cover under a sturdy table, and Hold On

MCQ 2. Why is throwing water onto an electrical fire extremely dangerous?  • a. Water makes the fire look bad  • b. Water conducts electricity, causing severe electrocution and spreading flames  • c. Water extinguishes it too fast  • d. None of these
Ans: b. Water conducts electricity, causing severe electrocution and spreading flames
MCQ 3. What is the emergency helpline number for the Rescue service in Pakistan?  • a. 1122  • b. 999  • c. 100  • d. 555

MCQ 4. Which safety equipment is mandatory for motorcyclists to prevent fatal head injuries?  • a. Sunglasses  • b. A certified, securely fastened safety helmet  • c. Leather gloves only  • d. A scarf
Ans: b. A certified, securely fastened safety helmet
Q1. Detail the essential safety rules that must be observed during a sudden outbreak of fire in a public building.

Ans: Sound the nearest fire alarm immediately, avoid panic, crawl low under smoke (since smoke rises), feel doorknobs with the back of the hand before opening, never use elevators, exit via marked emergency stairwells, assemble at the designated assembly point, and call the Fire Brigade (16 / 1122).
Q2. Explain the comprehensive safety precautions required during and immediately following an earthquake.

Ans: During tremors indoors: Drop, Cover, and Hold On beneath a sturdy desk away from glass windows and heavy bookcases. If outdoors: move into an open area away from electrical cables and tall facades. After tremors cease: check for gas leaks, shut off main electrical switches, and beware of secondary aftershocks.
Q3. Why is strict adherence to traffic signals and pedestrian regulations a moral civic obligation?

Ans: Traffic laws exist to safeguard human lives. Jumping red lights, over-speeding, or crossing roads carelessly jeopardizes not only the violator's life but also innocent motorists and pedestrians. True civic sense demands obeying rules even when traffic police are not watching.
Q4. What basic supplies and equipment should be contained in every household and school First Aid kit?

Ans: A standard First Aid kit must include sterile gauze pads, adhesive bandages, antiseptic liquid (e.g. Pyodine), medical tape, scissors, burn ointment, pain relief tablets, oral rehydration salts (ORS), a digital thermometer, and an updated emergency helpline directory.
► 8.2 Speaking: Structured Parliamentary Debate on 'Individual Civic Sense vs. Strict Government Enforcement'
► Civic Debate: Individual Responsibility vs Legal Enforcement

► 8.4 Writing: An Argumentative Essay on 'The Crucial Role of Civic Sense in Averting Public Disasters'
• Argumentative Essay: The Role of Civic Sense in Averting Disasters

A nation's civility and safety are profoundly mirrored in the everyday civic habits of its populace. Civic sense is not a passive philosophical concept; it is an active moral commitment to public welfare, orderliness, and mutual protection. When citizens lack civic consciousness, public spaces descend into chaos—motorists block emergency ambulance lanes, pedestrians jaywalk across dangerous highways, and buildings ignore essential fire exits. Tragically, this civic apathy turns minor emergencies into catastrophic losses of precious human lives. Conversely, when individuals internalize civic responsibility—respecting traffic signals, maintaining waste bins, knowing basic first aid, and obeying disaster management protocols—preventable tragedies are systematically averted. Therefore, instilling robust civic sense through school curricula and community training is the most powerful investment a nation can make to guarantee collective security and prosperity.

Dengue fever is a dangerous mosquito-borne disease that affects thousands of people during the monsoon season. It is spread by the Aedes mosquito which bites mostly during daytime. Mohtarma Fatima Jinnah, respectfully known as 'Madar-e-Millat' (Mother of the Nation), was born in Karachi in 1893. She was the beloved younger sister of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. She qualified as a dental surgeon, but gave up her career to support her brother in the freedom movement. She traveled throughout India, urging Muslim women to step forward for education and politics. After the creation of Pakistan, she worked tirelessly for the rehabilitation of refugees. Her life is an eternal inspiration of selfless patriotism and dedication.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS IX ENGLISH — UNIT 7LIFE SKILLS(7.1 The Secret of Success (Prose))
True success does not mean only earning money or fame; it means living a useful and honorable life.
Key to success: Hard work, honesty, self-discipline, and strong faith.
Goal Setting: We must set SMART goals (Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound).
Time Management: Time once lost can never be regained; do not waste time in useless activities.
Handling Failure: Never lose hope after failing; mistakes teach valuable lessons for ultimate success.
■  3. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
Discipline in classrooms and playgrounds builds responsible national character.
Accepting defeat with a smile is the true spirit of sportsmanship.
The school athlete trained diligently every evening on the running track.
Our cricket team proudly lifted the inter-school championship trophy.
Regular outdoor sports ensure sound health and physical fitness.
Victory in football requires coordinated teamwork rather than individual pride.
The marathon runner reached the finish line through grit and perseverance.
All players complied respectfully with the decisions of the referee.
Games provide wholesome recreation after long hours of academic study.
The young boxer shook hands cordially with his opponent after the bout.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
Q1:  What is the common misconception about success?
Ans:  People mistakenly think success only means having huge wealth, expensive cars, or luxurious mansions.
Q2:  What does the acronym SMART stand for in goal setting?
Ans:  S = Specific, M = Measurable, A = Achievable, R = Relevant, T = Time-bound.
Q3:  Why is time management essential for student success?
Ans:  Because students who plan their study hours complete their syllabus without stress and score high grades.
Q4:  How should a student view failure?
Ans:  A student should view failure as a stepping stone that points out weaknesses and prepares for future victory.
Q5:  State two daily habits that lead to success.
Ans:  1. Waking up early in the morning. 2. Planning daily study tasks with focus and honesty.
The gold medal was won by her.
The tournament will be organized by them.
The players were encouraged by the captain.

Time is the most precious treasure in human life. Money lost can be earned again, but lost seconds can never return. A student who respects time by studying regularly achieves top positions in board exams. Great leaders like Quaid-e-Azam strictly followed punctuality. Procrastination and laziness waste our youth. Therefore, every student must maintain a daily timetable for study, prayer, and sports.
THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS IX ENGLISH — UNIT 8PEOPLE AND PLACES(8.1 Ghazi's Diary | 8.4 The Miller of Dee | 8.6 Daffodils | 8.7 Health)
Ghazi traveled with his family to the breathtaking northern areas of Pakistan.
He visited Swat, Hunza, Skardu, Shangrila Lake, and the historic Baltit Fort.
He enjoyed cool fresh air, clear crystal streams, and fruit orchards.
► Part B: 'The Miller of the Dee' (Poem by Charles Mackay)
A happy miller lived beside the River Dee in England.
He sang all day: 'I envy nobody, no, not I, and nobody envies me!'
King Hal met him and confessed that despite his royal crown, he envied the miller's carefree, debt-free happiness.
Central Idea: Contentment, honest labor, and loving one's family bring true happiness.
The poet was wandering lonely as a cloud beside a lake.
He saw thousands of golden daffodils fluttering and dancing in the breeze.
Later, whenever he rests in a thoughtful or sad mood, the memory of daffodils flashes in his mind and fills his heart with joy.
• Poem 1: 'The Miller of the Dee' by Charles Mackay
Stanza: 'I earn my bread, quoth he; / I love my wife, I love my friend, / I love my children three; / I owe no penny I cannot pay...'
Context & Meaning: The miller explains the simple secrets of his joyful life: honest earnings, freedom from debt, and love for his family.
Stanza: 'For oft, when on my couch I lie / In vacant or in pensive mood, / They flash upon that inward eye / Which is the bliss of solitude...'
Reference: Written by William Wordsworth, the great poet of nature.
Context & Meaning: The sight of daffodils becomes a permanent source of pleasure. In moments of loneliness, the memory of nature brings pure delight.
■  3. WORDS, URDU MEANINGS & USE IN SENTENCES
The sacrifices of our national martyrs are immortal in Pakistan's history.
Our courageous armed forces defend the motherland against all hostilities.
Major Aziz Bhatti displayed extraordinary valor on the Lahore front.
The brave commander embraced martyrdom while defending the BRB canal.
The gallant soldiers repulsed enemy tank attacks with supreme resolve.
No sacrifice is too great when the sovereignty of the nation is at stake.
The courage of 1965 heroes is a glorious heritage for Pakistan's youth.
He was awarded Nishan-e-Haider, the highest posthumous military decoration.
Pakistan successfully crushed foreign military aggression in the September war.
The nation stood united with unshakable resolve during the wartime emergency.
► Dictation Words (20 Difficult Spellings for Practice)
Q1:  Which scenic valleys did Ghazi visit during his tour?
Ans:  Ghazi visited Swat Valley, Hunza Valley, and Skardu in Gilgit-Baltistan.
Q2:  Why was King Hal envious of the Miller of the Dee?
Ans:  Because the King carried heavy state worries, while the miller had a light, cheerful heart free of debt and envy.
Q3:  What did the poet William Wordsworth see beside the lake?
Ans:  He saw a huge crowd of thousands of golden daffodils fluttering and dancing in the cool breeze.
Q4:  What is meant by the 'inward eye' in the poem 'Daffodils'?
Ans:  The 'inward eye' refers to human spiritual imagination and sweet memory.
Q5:  What does Section 8.7 & 8.8 teach about healthy eating?
Ans:  It teaches that eating fresh fruits, green vegetables, and drinking clean water keeps the brain and body fit and active.
• Topic B: Quotation Marks in Direct Speech
2. King Hal asked, "Why are you so happy?"
3. Wordsworth wrote, "I wandered lonely as a cloud."

One day, the poet William Wordsworth was walking lonely beside a lake. Suddenly, he saw thousands of golden daffodils dancing under the trees in the gentle breeze. The sparkling waves of the lake also danced, but the daffodils outdid them in glee. The poet felt great happiness watching this charming scene. Later, whenever he lies on his couch in a thoughtful or sad mood, the memory of the daffodils flashes before his mind. His heart fills with pleasure, and he dances with the daffodils.

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESBOARD OF SECONDARY EDUCATION KARACHI (BSEK)S.S.C. ANNUAL EXAMINATIONS 2026 — GUESS / MODEL QUESTION PAPERENGLISH (COMPULSORY) — CLASS IX (SSC PART-I)
Time Allowed: 3 Hours  |  Maximum Marks: 100  |  Latest Board Pattern
Note: This section consists of 20 Multiple Choice Questions. All questions are compulsory. (1 Mark each)
1. The Last Sermon was delivered by the Holy Prophet (P.B.U.H) on the mount called:
(A) Mount Uhud     (B) Mount Hira     (C) Mount Arafat     (D) Mount Safa
2. According to the Last Sermon, an Arab has no superiority over a:
3. The Urs of Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai is celebrated every year on:
4. Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai invented a simple musical string instrument called:
5. Mohenjo-Daro was discovered by archaeologists in the year:
6. The historical site of Mohenjo-Daro is located in the district of:
7. The poem 'The Neem Tree' was written by the famous poetess:
(A) Sarojini Naidu     (B) Elsa Kazi     (C) Toru Dutt     (D) Sylvia Plath
8. In the poem, the Neem tree saves the traveler from the burning:
9. The cheerful Miller lived beside the River:
10. The Miller earned his livelihood by:
(A) Catching fish     (B) Grinding corn     (C) Farming wheat     (D) Cutting trees
11. Helen Keller lost her eyesight and hearing power at the age of:
(A) Two years     (B) Nineteen months     (C) Five years     (D) Seven years
12. The dedicated teacher who opened the world for Helen Keller was:
(A) Miss Sullivan     (B) Miss Florence     (C) Miss Clara     (D) Miss Jane
13. Malaria is transmitted to human beings by the bite of the female:
(A) Aedes mosquito     (B) Anopheles mosquito     (C) Culex mosquito     (D) Tsetse fly
14. Dengue virus is transmitted by the bite of the mosquito named:
15. In the poem 'Abou Ben Adhem', the angel was writing in a book of:
16. Abou Ben Adhem requested the angel to write his name as one who:
(A) Loves Allah     (B) Prays night and day     (C) Loves his fellow men     (D) Gives charity
17. Choose the correct passive voice: 'She writes a letter.'
(A) A letter was written by her.     (B) A letter is written by her.     (C) A letter has written by her.     (D) A letter is being wrote.
18. Choose the correct indirect speech: He said, 'I am unwell.'
(A) He said that he was unwell.     (B) He said that I am unwell.     (C) He told that he is unwell.     (D) He says that he was unwell.
19. Fill in with appropriate preposition: He died ___ malaria.
20. The comparative degree of the adjective 'good' is:
Q17: (B) A letter is written by her
Q18: (A) He said that he was unwell
Note: Answer any FIVE (5) of the following questions in 2 to 3 simple sentences. (4 Marks each)
Q1. What did the Holy Prophet (P.B.U.H) preach about the equality of human beings in the Last Sermon?
Model Answer: He declared that all mankind is from Adam, and an Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab, nor a white over a black. Superiority is based only on piety and good actions.
Q2. Why is Shah Abdul Latif called 'Bhitai' and what is 'Shah Jo Risalo'?
Model Answer: Shah Abdul Latif is called 'Bhitai' because he spent the final years of his life praying on a sand mound ('Bhit'). 'Shah Jo Risalo' is his famous collection of Sindhi mystical poetry.
Q3. What does the poetess Elsa Kazi urge human beings to learn from the Neem tree?
Model Answer: She urges human beings to bear difficulties with patience and selflessly provide shade, protection, and comfort to others, just as the Neem tree stands steadfast under the blazing sun.
Q4. Why is Mohenjo-Daro considered an advanced ancient civilization?
Model Answer: Because it was built over 5,000 years ago with wide brick-paved streets, multi-storey houses, a covered underground drainage system, and the famous Great Bath.
Q5. How did Miss Sullivan teach Helen Keller the names of physical objects?
Model Answer: Miss Sullivan spelled words into Helen's hand using touch finger alphabet and placed her other hand under running tap water to teach her the word 'W-A-T-E-R'.
Q6. Why was the Miller of the Dee happier than King Hal?
Model Answer: The Miller was happier because he worked hard, was contented with what he earned, owed no debt to anyone, and loved his family and neighbors honestly.
Q7. What are the primary symptoms and preventive steps for Dengue and Malaria?
Model Answer: Symptoms include high fever, severe joint pain, and headache. They can be prevented by using mosquito repellents, sleeping under bed nets, and eliminating stagnant water pools.
Q8. Why did Abou Ben Adhem's name top the angel's list of God's beloved people?
Model Answer: Because Abou Ben Adhem loved and selflessly served his fellow human beings. True love of Allah is expressed through compassionate service to mankind.
► Part-II: Grammar & Language in Use (Do as Directed) — [15 Marks]
Note: Attempt the following grammar questions according to the instructions in brackets. (1 Mark each)
1. The boy solved the puzzle easily. [Change into Passive Voice]   → Solution: The puzzle was solved easily by the boy.
2. The mechanic is repairing our car. [Change into Passive Voice]   → Solution: Our car is being repaired by the mechanic.
3. He said to me, 'I will help you tomorrow.' [Change into Indirect Speech]   → Solution: He told me that he would help me the next day.
4. Mother said to Aslam, 'Do not waste food.' [Change into Indirect Speech]   → Solution: Mother advised Aslam not to waste food.
5. She is ___ honest and hardworking student. [Insert suitable Article (a, an, the)]   → Solution: She is an honest and hardworking student.
6. The train arrived ___ the station on time. [Insert suitable Preposition (at, in, on)]   → Solution: The train arrived at the station on time.
7. He jumped ___ the swimming pool. [Insert suitable Preposition (in, into, onto)]   → Solution: He jumped into the swimming pool.
8. He plays football every evening. [Change into Interrogative Sentence]   → Solution: Does he play football every evening?
9. Aslam was driving a fast car. [Change into Negative Sentence]   → Solution: Aslam was not driving a fast car.
10. Karachi is the (large) city of Pakistan. [Use correct Degree of Adjective]   → Solution: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan.
11. This problem is (difficult) than that one. [Use correct Degree of Adjective]   → Solution: This problem is more difficult than that one.
12. Add a suitable prefix to the root word 'possible': [Form Opposite Word]   → Solution: Impossible
13. Add a suitable suffix to the root word 'care': [Form Adjective]   → Solution: Careful / Careless
14. Punctuate the sentence: alas we lost the match said ali [Punctuate and Capitalize]   → Solution: 'Alas! We lost the match,' said Ali.
15. Water (boil) at 100 degrees Celsius. [Use correct form of verb]   → Solution: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
► Part-III: Translation into Urdu / Sindhi — [5 Marks]

Q. Translate the following English passage into Urdu:"Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai was a noble saint and a great poet of Sindh. He loved poor working people, shepherds, and fishermen. He spent most of his time in prayers and composing spiritual verses. His shrine is at Bhit Shah, where thousands of devotees gather every year."

Model Answer (Alternative Note — 'Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai'): Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai was a revered mystic poet and saint of Sindh. He loved poor working people, shepherds, and fishermen. He spent most of his life in devotion to Allah and composed spiritual verses compiled in 'Shah Jo Risalo'. His annual Urs is celebrated with devotion at Bhit Shah.
► Q1. Detailed Composition / Essay Writing — [12 Marks]
Write a comprehensive essay of 120 to 150 words on ANY ONE of the following top-guess topics:
1. My Favorite Personality / Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah
2. Advantages and Disadvantages of Mobile Phones
► Complete Model Essay: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah

Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah is my favorite personality and the founding father of Pakistan. He was born on 25th December, 1876, in Karachi. After early schooling, he traveled to England where he studied law and qualified as the youngest barrister from Lincoln's Inn. He began his professional practice in Bombay and quickly became known for his honesty, brilliant legal intellect, and uncompromising integrity.

When the rights of Muslims were threatened in British India, the Quaid led the All-India Muslim League with extraordinary vision and political courage. He advocated the Two-Nation Theory, proving that Muslims possess a separate religious, cultural, and spiritual identity. Despite severe Hindu opposition and British diplomatic obstacles, he achieved an independent homeland on 14th August, 1947, strictly through peaceful and constitutional means.

His inspiring motto was 'Unity, Faith, and Discipline.' He worked day and night for the stability of Pakistan without caring for his failing health and passed away on 11th September, 1948. He remains an immortal hero for every Pakistani.
► Q2. Application to Headmaster OR Letter to Editor — [10 Marks]
► Model Application: Request for Full Fee Concession
The Master Sahib Model High School,
Subject: Application for Full Fee Concession

With utmost respect, I beg to submit that my father works as a daily-wage laborer in a local textile factory. His monthly income is barely sufficient to feed our large family of six members and pay for house rent.

Under these severe financial hardships, it has become impossible for my father to bear my school tuition fees and purchase new textbooks. I have always been a hardworking student and secured first position in Class VIII annual examinations with an 'A-1' grade.
I have a deep passion for education and wish to continue my studies. I therefore earnestly request you to grant me full fee concession so that I may pursue my education without disruption.
I shall be ever grateful for your kind sympathy and favor.
Class IX, Section B, Roll No. 25
► Q3. Summary of Poem / Central Idea — [8 Marks]
Write a concise summary of ANY ONE of the following poems:(1) The Neem Tree   (2) The Miller of the Dee   (3) Abou Ben Adhem
► Model Summary: The Neem Tree (By Elsa Kazi)
The poem 'The Neem Tree' is composed by the renowned poetess Elsa Kazi.
The Neem tree stands steadfast, green, and bold under the burning rays of the midday desert sun.
It selflessly provides cool, comforting shade and refreshing shelter to tired travelers and singing birds.
The poetess urges human beings to follow the noble example of the Neem tree in daily life.
Central Idea: We must bear life's trials with patience and sacrifice our comfort to serve and protect suffering humanity.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given at the end:Trees are the green lungs of our planet. They absorb harmful carbon dioxide gas from the atmosphere and release fresh oxygen, which is essential for the survival of all human and animal life. In addition to purifying the air, trees prevent soil erosion by binding the earth tightly with their deep root systems. They regulate rainfall, reduce the devastating impact of seasonal floods, and provide food and shelter to countless birds and wildlife. Forests also give us timber, rubber, and medicinal herbs. Unfortunately, rapid deforestation for building commercial housing societies is causing global warming and extreme heatwaves. It is our moral duty to plant more shade-bearing trees and protect our forests.
(1) Why are trees called the 'green lungs' of our planet?  →  Ans: Because they absorb harmful carbon dioxide and produce fresh life-giving oxygen for humans and animals.

(2) How do trees protect agricultural land from erosion and floods?  →  Ans: Their deep roots hold the topsoil tightly together, preventing erosion, and their canopies slow down heavy rainwater runoff.
(3) What harmful consequences are caused by deforestation?  →  Ans: Rapid deforestation leads to rising global warming, dangerous heatwaves, lack of rainfall, and destruction of wildlife habitats.
(4) Suggest an apt title for the passage.  →  Ans: Title: 'The Importance of Trees and Forests'

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS IX ENGLISH — UNIT 1ETHICS - CHARACTER BUILDING(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 1: ETHICS - CHARACTER BUILDING (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 1.1 Reading Comprehension: The Last Sermon of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W)
Pre-Reading Q1. What core moral qualities are essential for building personal character and a harmonious society?

Ans: Honesty, truthfulness, justice, universal equality, empathy, respect for human life and property, and fulfillment of covenants are essential moral virtues for individual and collective prosperity.
Pre-Reading Q2. What is the historical significance of the Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat-ul-Wida) in 10 A.H.?

Ans: It was the final pilgrimage performed by the Holy Prophet (S.A.W), during which he delivered a timeless charter of universal human rights on the plains of Mount Arafat to over 120,000 companions.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN SERMON TABLE
The sacred annual Islamic journey to the holy city of Makkah
The state of being holy, sacred, inviolable, and protected
The unjust practice of charging illegal interest on borrowed money
A solemn, binding agreement or promise made before Allah
The state of being higher in status or rank based on righteousness (Taqwa)
Something valuable placed in one's safe custody to be returned intact
Never to be broken, infringed, or dishonored
Universal brotherhood and mutual solidarity among all believers
The Last Sermon was delivered on the plains of Mount Arafat in 10 A.H.
Superiority in Islam is determined by racial heritage and ancestral wealth.
False (F) — Superiority is solely determined by piety, righteousness, and good deeds (Taqwa).
The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) declared human life, property, and honor sacred and inviolable.
All pre-Islamic blood feuds and interest transactions were abolished unconditionally.
Muslims are advised to abandon the Quran and Sunnah in modern times.
False (F) — The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) stated that holding fast to the Quran and Sunnah guarantees perpetual guidance.
MCQ 1. Where was the historic Farewell Sermon delivered?  • a. Madinah Munawwarah  • b. Mount Arafat (Jabal al-Rahmah)  • c. Cave of Hira  • d. Quba Mosque
MCQ 2. According to the sermon, an Arab has no superiority over a non-Arab except by:  • a. Lineage and tribe  • b. Material wealth  • c. Piety and righteousness (Taqwa)  • d. Physical strength

MCQ 3. What rights did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) emphasize regarding women?  • a. They must be treated with kindness, justice, and respect as trusted partners  • b. They have no legal status  • c. They should only work in farms  • d. None of these
Ans: a. They must be treated with kindness, justice, and respect as trusted partners

MCQ 4. What two sacred sources did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) leave behind for mankind's eternal guidance?  • a. Golden treasures and palaces  • b. The Holy Quran and the Sunnah  • c. Philosophical books  • d. Trade routes
Ans: b. The Holy Quran and the Sunnah
Q1. Why is the Last Sermon of the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) considered the first universal charter of human rights?

Ans: It unequivocally established universal human equality, abolished racial and tribal discrimination, guaranteed the sanctity of life, property, and honor, protected women's legal rights, abolished usury and slavery exploitation, and affirmed accountability before Allah centuries before modern declarations.
Q2. Explain the Islamic concept of universal equality as outlined in the sermon.

Ans: The Holy Prophet (S.A.W) declared that all mankind is descended from Adam, and Adam was created from dust. An Arab possesses no superiority over a non-Arab, nor does a white person have superiority over a black person, except through piety and good moral conduct.
Q3. What instructions did the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) give regarding the treatment of women and servants?

Ans: He enjoined believers to treat women with kindness and fairness, recognizing their mutual rights and dignity. Regarding subordinates and servants, he ordered that they should be fed with what masters eat and clothed with what masters wear, treating them as brothers in faith.
Q4. What was the momentous concluding question the Holy Prophet (S.A.W) asked the congregation?

Ans: He asked: 'O people, have I faithfully conveyed the Message of Allah to you?' The congregation resoundingly cried: 'Yes, you have!' Whereupon the Prophet raised his forefinger to heaven and exclaimed: 'O Allah, bear witness!'
► 1.2 Speaking: Sharing Information and Ideas on Universal Human Rights
► Implementing Farewell Sermon Principles in School Life
Situation: Classroom discussion among students on implementing the principles of the Last Sermon in modern school and civic life:
Bilal: How can we practically apply the teachings of the Farewell Sermon in our daily school environment?
Zain: By treating every classmate with absolute equality regardless of their socio-economic background, ethnicity, or language.
Hamza: Furthermore, by respecting everyone's belongings and standing up against bullying, we protect the sanctity of honor and property emphasized by the Holy Prophet (S.A.W).
Bilal: Indeed, living by justice and empathy is the true tribute to the Prophet's universal guidance.

► 1.4 Writing: Formal Letter to the Editor on Promoting Civic Ethics and Cleanliness
• Formal Letter to the Editor on Civic Ethics & Cleanliness
Subject: Urgent Need for Civic Ethics and Neighborhood Cleanliness Awareness

Through the esteemed columns of your widely circulated newspaper, I wish to draw the attention of the civic authorities and general public towards the deteriorating sanitation conditions and lack of civic responsibility in our residential sectors.
Heaps of uncollected garbage, overflowing drain lines, and open burning of plastic waste are creating severe health hazards and respiratory diseases among school children and the elderly.

As taught by our ethical traditions, cleanliness is half of faith. It is imperative that the municipal corporation ensures daily trash collection while citizens practice civic discipline by using designated waste bins.
I urge the authorities to initiate a community cleanliness awareness campaign and impose strict penalties on illegal dumping to safeguard our environment.
► 1.5 Study Skills: Systematic Editing and Proofreading Checklist
1. Capitalization: Check proper nouns, days of the week, months, book titles, and the first letter of sentences.
2. Subject-Verb Agreement: Ensure singular subjects take singular verbs and plural subjects take plural verbs.
3. Punctuation Marks: Verify quotation marks for direct speech, commas in compound sentences, and terminal full stops.
4. Spelling & Homophones: Look out for easily confused words like their/there/they're, its/it's, and accept/except.
5. Sentence Flow: Read paragraphs aloud to ensure smooth transitions between topic and concluding sentences.
► 1.6 Fun: Designing an Informative Cultural Travel Brochure
• Choose an iconic historical destination (e.g., Makli Necropolis, Mohen-jo-Daro, or Gorakh Hill).
• Include an inspiring slogan: 'Discover the Cradle of Ancient Civilization!'
• List key visitor attractions, ideal travel seasons, local handicrafts, and accommodation tips.

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS IX ENGLISH — UNIT 2ROLE MODEL(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
► 2.1 Reading Comprehension: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai
■ PRE-READING QUESTIONS & ROLE MODEL QUALITIES DISCUSSION
Pre-Reading Q1. Who is considered a true role model in our society?
Ans: A true role model is a person of noble character, profound spiritual wisdom, humility, universal compassion, and selfless devotion who inspires generations to live peacefully and harmoniously.
Pre-Reading Q2. What do you already know about the great saint-poet Shah Abdul Latif of Bhit?
Ans: Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai was a renowned Sufi saint and poet of Sindh whose mystic poetry, compiled in 'Shah Jo Risalo', conveys the universal message of divine love, human equality, and peace.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: SUFI TERMINOLOGY & CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS TABLE
A spiritual seeker who pursues direct communion and divine love with Allah
The revered burial tomb of a saint visited by pilgrims
A five-stringed musical instrument invented by Shah Latif for devotional music
The annual death anniversary and spiritual festival celebrated at a saint's shrine
A collection of literary or poetic works assembled into a single volume
The monumental collection of Shah Abdul Latif's mystic poetry across 30 Surs
A sand dune / mound of earth near Hala where the saint settled in meditation
A sequence of musical notes that produce a harmonious and soul-stirring sound
Shah Abdul Latif was born in Hala Haveli in 1689 (1102 A.H.).
Shah Latif belonged to a prominent family descended from the Holy Prophet (S.A.W).
Shah Latif was interested only in courtly politics and worldly wealth.
False (F) — From youth, he was spiritually inclined, fond of prayer, and lived in monastic simplicity.
The musical instrument invented by Shah Latif is known as the Tambooro (Tanpura).
Shah Jo Risalo has been translated into English, Urdu, and many international languages.
MCQ 1. Where is the resting place (shrine) of Shah Abdul Latif located?  • a. Sehwan Sharif  • b. Bhit Shah (Matiari District)  • c. Thatta  • d. Sukkur
MCQ 2. What does the word 'Bhit' mean in Sindhi?  • a. A flowing river  • b. A mound or sand dune  • c. A green garden  • d. A stone fort
Ans: b. A mound or sand dune
MCQ 3. Which ruler of Sindh built the magnificent shrine over Shah Latif's tomb?  • a. Ghulam Shah Kalhoro  • b. Jam Nizamuddin  • c. Talpur Mirs  • d. Akbar the Great
MCQ 4. When is the annual Urs of Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai celebrated?  • a. 1st Shawwal  • b. 14th Safar  • c. 12th Rabi-ul-Awwal  • d. 10th Muharram
Q1. Why is Shah Abdul Latif called 'Bhittai' (the Saint of the Mound)?

Ans: When his father passed away, Shah Latif left his ancestral town and settled on a quiet sand mound (known as 'Bhit' in Sindhi) near Hala to spend his days in contemplation, prayer, and writing mystic poetry. Hence, he is revered as Shah Abdul Latif of Bhit (Bhittai).
Q2. What is the central theme and spiritual message of 'Shah Jo Risalo'?

Ans: The central message of 'Shah Jo Risalo' is selfless love for the Divine Creator, universal human brotherhood, patience, endurance, and empathy for the oppressed. Through heroic folk heroines (Marvi, Sassui, Sohni, Momal), he symbolizes the soul's passionate quest for spiritual truth.
Q3. Describe the origin and special musical feature of Shah Latif's 'Tambooro'.

Ans: Finding traditional musical instruments complicated for expressing mystic ecstasy, Shah Latif simplified the instrument by creating a five-stringed version named 'Tambooro', designed so that anyone could play and sing spiritual verses with ease.
Q4. How is the annual Urs of Shah Latif celebrated at Bhit Shah?

Ans: Every year on the 14th of Safar, hundreds of thousands of pilgrims, scholars, and musicians gather at Bhit Shah. Folk singers dressed in black robes sing verses from Shah Jo Risalo with deep spiritual fervor, and literary conferences celebrate his cultural legacy.
► 2.2 Speaking: Asking and Answering Questions on Cultural Heritage
► Cultural Significance of the Urs at Bhit Shah
Situation: Dialogue between two students discussing their visit to the Urs and museum at Bhit Shah:
Asif: Have you ever attended the annual Urs celebration at Bhit Shah?
Kamran: Yes, I visited Bhit Shah with my uncle last year during Safar, and the spiritual ambiance was truly mesmerizing.
Asif: What impressed you most about the shrine and the gathering?
Kamran: The soulful singing of Shah's poetry by traditional Faqirs playing the Tambooro, alongside the message of universal tolerance that brings people of all faiths together.
► 2.3 Language Practice: Modals for Ability ('Can', 'Could', 'Be Able To') and Suffixes
■ EXERCISE 1: MODALS OF ABILITY ('CAN', 'COULD', 'BE ABLE TO') TABLE
Folk musicians can recite all 30 Surs of Shah Jo Risalo by heart.
A person with hatred in their heart cannot understand mystic poetry.
Shah Latif could compose profound verses spontaneously in his youth.
The disciples were able to compile his verses into a sacred manuscript.
Students will be able to appreciate Sufi literature by visiting Bhit Shah.
Compiling Shah Jo Risalo was a historic literary achievement.
His mystic verses serve as an eternal inspiration for humanity.
The atmosphere around the shrine is peaceful and serene.
The saint dedicated his entire life to selfless devotion.
His timeless message of brotherhood is universally reverable.
► 2.4 Writing: A Comprehensive Narrative Essay on 'Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai: The Crown of Sufi Poetry'
• Comprehensive Narrative Essay: The Saint of Bhit

Shah Abdul Latif Bhittai stands as the most towering spiritual and literary figure in the history of Sindh. Born in 1689 at Hala Haveli into a noble family descended from the Holy Prophet (S.A.W), he exhibited deep spiritual introspection, piety, and love for nature from an early age. As a young man, he traveled extensively across Sindh, Balochistan, and neighboring lands with ascetics and dervishes, keenly observing the hardships, culture, and pure languages of common villagers and desert folk. Upon his return, he made a peaceful sand dune (Bhit) his permanent abode, spending his days in prayer, musical contemplation, and composing soul-stirring verses in the Sindhi language. His immortal collection, 'Shah Jo Risalo', uses indigenous folk romances such as Umar Marvi and Sassui Punhun as allegories to teach spiritual endurance, patriotism, and selfless devotion to Allah. Today, his majestic shrine at Bhit Shah remains a radiant beacon of peace, attracting millions who find solace in his universal message of divine love and human fraternity.
► 2.5 Study Skills: Structuring a Biographical Outline into Cohesive Paragraphs
Chronological Order: Arrange events from birth, lineage, early education, major life turning points, to lasting legacy.
Transitional Words: Use connectors like 'From his early youth', 'Subsequently', 'Consequently', and 'In his later years'.
Evidence & Quotations: Incorporate known quotes and historical dates to provide factual depth to historical accounts.
► 2.6 Fun: Recitation & Reflection on Shah Latif's Universal Prayer (Sur Sarang)
"O Lord, may Thou forever make Sindh prosperous and fertile,
O my Sweet Sustainer, let Thy boundless blessings shower over the entire universe!"

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS IX ENGLISH — UNIT 3EDUCATION AND CAREERS(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 3: EDUCATION AND CAREERS (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 3.1 Reading Comprehension: Chasing Dreams & The Neem Tree (Poem by Mrs. Elsa Kazi)
Pre-Reading Q1. What sacrifices and dedication are required to achieve one's career dreams?
Ans: Achieving professional dreams requires relentless hard work, academic discipline, financial perseverance, time management, and the moral resilience to overcome obstacles.
Pre-Reading Q2. How does a green tree standing under the scorching sun symbolize selfless service?
Ans: A tree endures the burning heat of the sun without complaint, providing cool shade, soothing shelter, and fresh oxygen to weary travelers, symbolizing selfless sacrifice for others.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: CONTEXTUAL MEANINGS IN UNIT TABLE
A strong hope, desire, or ambition to achieve high goals
Persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in success
Extremely hot and burning (referring to fierce summer sunlight)
Firm, steadfast, and refusing to give up under hardship
Gently calm, relieve pain, or comfort someone in distress
Concerned more with the needs and wishes of others than one's own
Complete devotion and commitment to a noble task or purpose
Express the meaning of a poem or text using clear, simple words
Jameel worked tirelessly to pass his medical entrance examination.
The Neem Tree is written by the German-born poetess Mrs. Elsa Kazi.
The poet describes the Neem tree as weak and complaining about the summer heat.
False (F) — The poem portrays the Neem tree as a bold, unyielding protector that shields others from heat.
Education and hard work enable youth from rural backgrounds to attain high careers.
A compare-and-contrast essay examines only the similarities between two topics.
False (F) — It analyzes both similarities (compare) and differences (contrast).
MCQ 1. Who wrote the famous philosophical poem 'The Neem Tree'?  • a. William Wordsworth  • b. Mrs. Elsa Kazi  • c. Leigh Hunt  • d. Robert Frost

MCQ 2. What quality of the Neem tree does the poetess urge human beings to emulate?  • a. Growing tall quickly  • b. Bearing hardships patiently to protect and comfort others  • c. Producing bitter fruit  • d. Shedding leaves in winter
Ans: b. Bearing hardships patiently to protect and comfort others
MCQ 3. What career dream did Jameel pursue despite financial constraints?  • a. Merchant navy officer  • b. Medical doctor serving his village community  • c. Politician  • d. Banker
Ans: b. Medical doctor serving his village community
MCQ 4. What does the Neem tree do when the burning sun blazes down?  • a. Withers and dies  • b. Stands bold, unruffled, and offers soothing green shade  • c. Bends to the ground  • d. Asks for water
Ans: b. Stands bold, unruffled, and offers soothing green shade
Q1. What is the central philosophical theme of the poem 'The Neem Tree'?

Ans: The central theme is selflessness, endurance, and moral nobility. The Neem tree stands tall under the blazing, scorching sun without complaint, offering cooling shade and protection to travelers. The poet challenges human beings to rise above selfish desires and dedicate their lives to shielding and uplifting suffering humanity.
Q2. How did Jameel demonstrate perseverance in 'Chasing Dreams'?

Ans: Coming from a humble rural family with limited resources, Jameel studied under kerosene lamps, traveled miles to attend college, worked part-time jobs, and maintained unwavering focus until he successfully gained admission to medical college and became a doctor.
Q3. Explain the metaphorical comparison between man and the Neem tree in the poem.

Ans: The poetess asks: 'Could man be as bold as thou and save / His fellow man from every woe?' She compares the physical endurance of the tree with the spiritual strength required of human beings to bear life's trials so they may relieve the sorrows of others.
Q4. What role does family support play in achieving academic success according to the text?

Ans: Family encouragement, emotional sacrifices, and belief in a child's potential provide the crucial foundation that empowers students to overcome self-doubt and succeed in competitive academic fields.
► 3.2 Speaking: Expressing Personal Wishes and Career Aspirations
► Expressing Future Wishes and Biomedical Goals
Situation: Dialogue between two students discussing their future higher education goals and service to society:
Nadia: I wish to pursue biomedical engineering after intermediate college.
Hira: That is an inspiring ambition! What motivated you to choose this specialized field?
Nadia: I want to design affordable prosthetic limbs and medical devices for underprivileged patients in our government hospitals.
Hira: That aligns beautifully with the message of 'The Neem Tree'—using one's professional knowledge for selfless human welfare!
► 3.3 Language Practice: Five Types of Sentences and Use of Articles ('A', 'An', 'The')
■ EXERCISE 1: FIVE TYPES OF SENTENCES TABLE
States a fact, opinion, or information
The Neem tree produces soothing shade in the hottest summer.
Could man be as steadfast and selfless as the Neem tree?
Expresses a command, request, or advice
Work diligently to achieve your educational goals.
Expresses strong emotion or surprise (ends with '!')
How majestic and green the Neem tree looks under the sun!
Expresses a wish, blessing, or prayer
May you succeed in fulfilling all your career dreams!
Used before singular countable nouns starting with consonant sound
Jameel bought a medical dictionary for his studies.
Used before singular countable nouns starting with vowel sound
Elsa Kazi was an exceptional German-Pakistani poetess.
Definite article: unique objects, specific things, superlative degree
The sun blazes down fiercely upon the green branches.
No article before abstract nouns or plural general nouns
Education brings prosperity and wisdom to society.
► 3.4 Writing: Compare and Contrast Essay on 'Rural vs Urban Educational Opportunities'
• Compare & Contrast Essay: Rural vs Urban Educational Opportunities

Education is the universal gateway to social and economic empowerment, yet the educational experiences of rural and urban students in Pakistan present striking similarities and significant contrasts. Both rural and urban learners share the identical curriculum, aspire to achieve prestigious professional careers, and possess immense intellectual talent. However, urban students enjoy modern infrastructure, including well-equipped science laboratories, computer facilities, high-speed internet, and qualified subject specialists. In contrast, rural students frequently face long commuting distances, teacher shortages, and limited career counseling, requiring extraordinary personal resilience to compete. Bridging this educational divide through digital classrooms and rural infrastructure is essential to ensure equal educational opportunities for every Pakistani youth.
► 3.5 Study Skills: Interpreting Academic Line and Bar Graphs
1. Title & Axes: Identify the chart title, what the horizontal X-axis represents (e.g. Years), and what the vertical Y-axis measures (e.g. Literacy %).
2. Key Trends: Look for upward trajectories (growth), downward dips, or plateau periods.
3. Comparative Insights: Compare two data series (e.g., Male vs Female literacy growth) and summarize findings into 3 concise sentences.
• 'Student Spotlight': Highlighting academic achievers and science fair winners.
• 'Poetry Corner': Showcasing student reflections on Elsa Kazi's 'The Neem Tree'.
• 'Career Compass': Monthly overview of emerging degrees in Artificial Intelligence and Renewable Energy.

content.text: THE MASTER SAHIB EDUCATIONAL SERIESCLASS IX ENGLISH — UNIT 4PAKISTAN AND NATIONAL PRIDE(Complete Solved Textbook Exercises)
■  UNIT 4: PAKISTAN AND NATIONAL PRIDE (SOLVED TEXTBOOK EXERCISES)
► 4.1 Reading Comprehension: The Great Visionaries (Quaid-e-Azam & Allama Iqbal) & Mohen-jo-Daro
Pre-Reading Q1. What distinguishes a visionary political leader from an ordinary politician?

Ans: A visionary leader possesses foresight, unshakeable integrity, moral conviction, and the ability to unite diverse people to achieve freedom, justice, and statehood without compromising on ethical principles.
Pre-Reading Q2. What is the historical significance of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization at Mohen-jo-Daro?
Ans: Dating back 5,000 years, Mohen-jo-Daro showcases world-class Bronze Age urban planning, baked-brick architecture, straight grid streets, and advanced covered underground drainage systems.
■ VOCABULARY EXERCISE 2: HISTORICAL & CIVIC TERMS TABLE
A leader with clear, inspiring ideas and foresight about the future
The fundamental right of a nation to determine its own political destiny
Supreme independent authority and governance of a state
Strict adherence to rules, order, and principled conduct
The scientific study of ancient human history through excavating ruins
A massive, watertight brick pool excavated at Mohen-jo-Daro for public or ritual bathing
Clay bricks hardened in kilns, providing enduring structural strength
Enduring ideas, achievements, and values left behind for future generations
Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah founded Pakistan through constitutional and democratic struggle.
Allama Muhammad Iqbal delivered his historic address proposing an autonomous Muslim state at Allahabad in 1930.
Mohen-jo-Daro had chaotic and unplanned mud huts with no sanitation.
False (F) — It had sophisticated grid-pattern streets and underground covered drainage.
Quaid-e-Azam's motto for the nation is 'Unity, Faith, and Discipline'.
In his 11th August 1947 address, the Quaid guaranteed absolute religious freedom for all citizens of Pakistan.
MCQ 1. In which year did Allama Iqbal deliver his historic presidential address at Allahabad?  • a. 1940  • b. 1930  • c. 1920  • d. 1947

MCQ 2. What famous guiding motto was given to the nation by Quaid-e-Azam?  • a. Power, Wealth, and Glory  • b. Unity, Faith, and Discipline  • c. Speed, Strength, and Honor  • d. Peace, Silence, and Work
Ans: b. Unity, Faith, and Discipline
MCQ 3. Where is the ancient archaeological site of Mohen-jo-Daro located?  • a. Rawalpindi District  • b. Larkana District, Sindh  • c. Sahiwal District  • d. Peshawar

MCQ 4. What unique sanitary feature astounded British archaeologists at Mohen-jo-Daro?  • a. Deep ocean canals  • b. Covered underground brick drainage systems in every street  • c. Iron pipes  • d. Plastic tanks
Ans: b. Covered underground brick drainage systems in every street
Q1. How did Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah articulate the vision for an independent Pakistan?

Ans: Quaid-e-Azam articulated that Muslims of the subcontinent constitute a distinct nation with their own civilization, culture, values, and laws. Through steadfast constitutional negotiation, integrity, and democratic mobilization, he united millions to establish Pakistan as an independent homeland.
Q2. What was the core message of Quaid-e-Azam's historic 11th August 1947 address to the Constituent Assembly?

Ans: He declared: 'You are free; you are free to go to your temples, you are free to go to your mosques or to any other place of worship in this State of Pakistan. You may belong to any religion or caste or creed—that has nothing to do with the business of the State.' He guaranteed equal citizenship and rights to all minorities.
Q3. Explain the significance of Allama Iqbal's poetry in awakening the Muslim nation.

Ans: Allama Iqbal's philosophical poetry (such as 'Bang-e-Dra', 'Bal-e-Jibril', and 'Asrar-e-Khudi') inspired the youth with the concept of 'Khudi' (self-realization), urging them to break the chains of intellectual servitude, pursue dynamic action, and rediscover their noble heritage.
Q4. Describe the advanced urban planning features discovered at Mohen-jo-Daro.

Ans: Mohen-jo-Daro featured straight broad avenues intersecting at right angles, multi-storey baked-brick houses with private courtyards and bathrooms, the Great Bath, large public granaries for grain storage, and covered street gutters with inspection traps.
► 4.2 Speaking: Academic Discussion on National Identity and Historical Heritage
► Lessons of the Pakistan Movement for 21st Century
Situation: Group dialogue between students discussing the lessons of the Pakistan Movement for the 21st century:
Tariq: What is the greatest lesson we can learn from Quaid-e-Azam's life and leadership?
Mansoor: His unwavering honesty, devotion to constitutional law, and absolute refusal to compromise on justice and principles.
Tariq: How can our generation uphold Allama Iqbal's concept of 'Khudi'?
Mansoor: By excelling in modern science, technology, and literature, maintaining self-respect, and dedicating our skills to national sovereignty.
► 4.3 Language Practice: Active & Passive Voice Transformation and Prefixes
■ EXERCISE 1: ACTIVE TO PASSIVE VOICE TRANSFORMATION TABLE
Pakistan was founded by Quaid-e-Azam in 1947.
Allama Iqbal wrote inspiring national poems.
Inspiring national poems were written by Allama Iqbal.
Archaeologists discovered the ruins of Mohen-jo-Daro.
The ruins of Mohen-jo-Daro were discovered by archaeologists.
Citizens must follow traffic and civic rules.
Traffic and civic rules must be followed by citizens.
The government is preserving historical monuments.
Historical monuments are being preserved by the government.
We will celebrate Independence Day with zeal.
Independence Day will be celebrated with zeal by us.
■ EXERCISE 2: PREFIXES (UN-, IN-, DIS-, IM-, MIS-) TABLE
We must eliminate unequal social opportunities.
The Quaid fought courageously against political injustice.
Responsible citizens never disobey state laws.
Dedication makes seemingly impossible goals achievable.
Do not misunderstand the principles of freedom.
► 4.4 Writing: Formal Application to the Principal for Issuance of Character Certificate
Subject: Application for Issuance of Character / School Leaving Certificate
With utmost respect, I beg to submit that I have been a regular student of Class IX in your prestigious institution during the current academic session.

Due to my father's recent official transfer to Hyderabad, our entire family is relocating next week. Consequently, I need to take admission in a government high school in Hyderabad to continue my secondary education.
I have cleared all school dues, returned library books, and maintained an unblemished academic and disciplinary record throughout my stay here.
I kindly request you to issue my Character Certificate and School Leaving Certificate at your earliest convenience so that I may complete my admission process on time.
► 4.5 Study Skills: Active Listening Strategies for Academic Lectures
1. Listen for Signpost Words: Focus on transition markers like 'firstly', 'the primary reason', 'in contrast', and 'most importantly'.
2. Record Dates & Proper Names: Note down key historical figures, locations, and milestones in bullet format.
3. Summarize Core Argument: At the conclusion of the lecture, write down the central thesis in 2 sentences.
► 4.6 Fun: Role Play Excerpt from Quaid-e-Azam's Golden Words
"With faith, discipline and selfless devotion to duty, there is nothing worthwhile that you cannot achieve."
